\\\"related_chapter\\\", \\\"content\\\": \\\"[EXCERPT extracted-character range 0:12142]\\\\n# K-TOOLS-006：正确性 Oracle：函数参考、状态变形与服务契约\\\\n\\\\n正确性验证需要一组互补、具有明确前提且能够拒绝已知错误的 oracle。函数参考约束数值函数，变形关系约束执行组织改变后的语义，概率 oracle 约束分布，协议与资源 oracle 约束身份、事件、所有权和终态。它们提供不同范围的证据，不能由一条看起来合理的最终文本相互替代。\\\\n\\\\n## 任务契约、身份与判定域\\\\n\\\\n设任务契约 C 包括输入规范化、模型与权重身份、processor、位置与 mask、数值策略、采样和停止规则、协议终态与资源责任。一次执行尝试记为 R=(r,g,x,θ,ε,h,Obs)：r 是请求身份，g 是执行尝试代次，x 是规范化输入，θ 是模型和采样配置，ε 是环境，h 是执行历史，Obs 是观测。物理槽 s 的分配代次 e 与请求尝试 g 是两个独立坐标；同一请求重试可以改变 g，同一槽被另一个请求取得可以改变 e。\\\\n\\\\n一个 oracle 定义为 O=(D,Pre,Rel,Ev,Cmp)。D 是输入与状态域；Pre 是合法前提；Rel 是应成立的关系；Ev 指明可用证据及其覆盖；Cmp 指明比较算法、单位和容差。另附独立性声明 Ind：预期值或判断规则不能依赖正在检验的故障组件。例如参考可以共用权重文件，但验证分页索引时不能共用被测页表；验证 processor 时不能共用同一个 processor。\\\\n\\\\n应检查实例集合 Ω 必须由任务预先给出，不能从实际返回的成功记录反推。每个实例进入以下一种结果：PASS 为前提相容、证据完整且关系成立；FAIL 为具有有效失败见证；INVALID 为参考定义、版本或比较单位已知不相容；UNKNOWN 为缺少必要证据而无法判定。Ω 为空不能借全称命题的空集真值报告完成；负对照未被拒绝时，检查器不具备该维度的判别资格。\\\\n\\\\n需要区分两种身份不符：把另一个模型版本的参考误拿来比较，属于比较前提 INVALID；在已经冻结、身份可信的任务表下，服务把旧尝试结果提交为当前结果，则违反输出归属义务，属于 FAIL。若连日志归属都无法确认，应保留 UNKNOWN，不能直接归因于引擎数值错误。\\\\n\\\\n状态记录按所检验机制携带请求 r、尝试 g、槽及其代次 (s,e)、分支、逻辑位置 t、对象或表示版本 v 和事件序号。没有一个固定短键可以替代所有层次。例如一次请求可能使用多页，不能要求其所有对象共享一个槽号；终止记录也不能用终止发生时槽的当前拥有者替换产生该尝试的原始身份。\\\\n\\\\n## 函数参考与合法域\\\\n\\\\n固定函数写为 y=F_C(x;θ)。x 包括 token 或特征、逻辑位置、有效输入、可见集合、padding 和缓存状态；θ 包括权重、adapter、归一化、量化参数和推理模式。输入规范化、tokenizer/template、模型参数、位置、mask、dtype 与量化契约必须相容。改变窗口、adapter、stop 规则或前处理，可能已经改变任务函数，不能用放宽数值容差处理。\\\\n\\\\n对有限参考 b 和观测 a，逐元素容差可定义为 |a−b|≤atol+rtol·|b|；向量比较也可声明 ‖a−b‖∞≤atol+rtol·‖b‖∞。这两种关系不同，应固定使用哪一种。atol 与张量的物理或数值尺度相联系；参考接近零时，不能只依赖相对误差。NaN、正负无穷和空张量由契约单独处理，默认不把 NaN 与 NaN 当作通过，也不把 inf−inf 的结果交给普通容差分支。\\\\n\\\\n浮点归约重排、批量与切片路径可能产生差异，因此数学等价不要求跨后端逐位一致。但容差通过也不证明最终选择相同。设参考最高两个分数 z(1)≥z(2)，各分数观测误差均不超过 ε。最高分最多下降 ε，竞争者最多上升 ε，因此 z(1)−z(2)>2ε 足以保证 argmax 不变。等号处不能保证，margin 更小时应报告证书不成立，再检查实际选择或提高参考精度，不能自动宣称实现错误或质量合格。\\\\n\\\\n低位路径先验证固定量化函数，再评估原模型质量。对 r=S(q−Z)，输入参数为 (S1,Z1)、(S2,Z2)，输出为 (S3,Z3)。长度 N 的整数点积为\\\\n\\\\nA=Σj(q1j−Z1)(q2j−Z2)\\\\n =Σj q1j q2j−Z1Σj q2j−Z2Σj q1j+NZ1Z2。\\\\n\\\\n若 bias 使用 Sbias=S1S2、Zbias=0，整数 bias b 加入 A。理想输出码坐标为 q3*=Z3+(S1S2/S3)(A+b)，实际输出还要按契约做舍入、饱和及激活钳位。q3* 通常不是整数，不能省略这些步骤后声称得到实际输出码。独立参考可先逐项解码相乘，再与补偿式核对；漏零点补偿、多加 bias、错误处理负数中点舍入应成为能触发差异的反例。该参考验证同制品计算，不证明校准分布上的模型质量，也不把特定 ARM 中间累加条件推广为任意 INT8 硬件保证。\\\\n\\\\n参考还需要状态独立。分页检查从逻辑 token 历史重建输入；前缀缓存检查从相同不可变前缀独立重算；取消检查从冻结的请求义务与资源票据出发。直接复用待测缓存加速参考，会失去对应缓存索引与内容身份的独立证据。\\\\n\\\\n## 变形关系与状态推进\\\\n\\\\n变形关系记为 MR=(Pre,T,Q,≈)：当 Pre(x) 成立时，Q(F(x))≈F(T(x))。T 改变执行组织，Q 恢复结果身份或顺序，≈ 是精确关系或声明的容差。改变采样随机流、模型版本或可见窗口后，原来的文本等价关系可能不再适用。\\\\n\\\\n批次置换要求 F(π(X))=π(F(X))，比较前先按请求与分支还原结果。它检查 batch 行映射、采样参数和输出归属，不要求不同 batch 几何的浮点结果逐位相同。取消或压紧一行时，token、length、adapter、RNG、KV 句柄和输出目标必须来自同一身份快照；只移动 token tensor 会把一行拼成不同请求的混合状态。\\\\n\\\\n分块 prefill 保持完整逻辑 token、全局位置和可见集合不变，只改变提交边界。普通因果 self-attention 的合法集合为 A_t={j：j 属于同一请求且 0≤j≤t}。第二个 chunk 的局部行号不能重置模型逻辑位置。一个可复算的小模型取 token=(1,2,3,4)、位置权重=(1,3,5,7)，全局参考为 1+6+15+28=50。按 [0,2)、[2,4) 分块仍为 50；第二块错误重置位置后得到 1+6+3+12=22。这个模型检验位置推进，不模拟真实 attention 数值。\\\\n\\\\n物理页置换改变 locate(l,j)，但不改变逻辑位置 j、内容与表示元数据。前缀命中等价要求 tokenizer/template、模型与 adapter、位置规则、前缀内容和 KV 表示身份相容；scale、zero point 或分组改变后，不能拿旧码配新尺度并继续声称同一函数。参考关注合法命中后的语义，不要求缓存策略一定命中。\\\\n\\\\n取消后使用回收槽的请求，应与从全新槽执行具有相同业务语义和资源终态。合法复用要求旧生命期的全部实际访问结束；递增 g 或 e 只能拒绝旧结果提交，不能阻止旧 DMA 写同一地址。测试需控制旧工作晚到、新工作先返回、取消与提交竞争、部分传输完成等时序。随机压力有发现价值，确定性时序便于归因，两者的一次通过都不能证明全部竞态消除。\\\\n\\\\n边界由机制选择：空输入、单 token、跨页、非整除尾部、零长度 chunk、最大合法长度以及空可见集合各有不同前提。合法零长度 chunk 不推进状态；所有 chunk 的有效区间仍须不重叠、无缺口地覆盖输入。空求和参考返回零，不等于空请求义务集合已经验证成功。\\\\n\\\\n## 概率 oracle 与 CDF 边界\\\\n\\\\n对离散概率 p，先要求词表非空、p_i≥0、Σp_i=1，且正概率支持集包含于任务允许集合。约束采样若合法集合质量为零，应按契约失败，不能静默回退到被禁止的 token。\\\\n\\\\n令 C_−1=0，C_i=Σj≤i p_j。对 u∈[0,1)，选择首个满足 C_i>u 的位置，即唯一满足 C_i−1≤u<C_i 的非空区间。这是左闭右开的规则；零概率项的区间为空，必须跳过。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 InverseCDF(p,u)\\\\n输入：非空离散概率向量 p；u∈[0,1)\\\\n输出：所选 token 下标，或输入/数值覆盖错误\\\\n1 核对每个 p[i] 非负、总和为 1，且 u 在声明范围内\\\\n2 c←0\\\\n3 对 i=0,…,V−1：\\\\n    c←c+p[i]\\\\n    若 u<c：返回 i\\\\n4 报告累计覆盖错误；不得无条件返回最后一个 token\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\np=(1/5,3/10,1/2) 的区间依次为 [0,1/5)、[1/5,1/2)、[1/2,1)。因此 u=0 选择 0，u=1/5 选择 1，u=1/2 选择 2。p=(0,1)、u=0 必须选择 1。p=(0,1/5,0,4/5,0)、u=1/5 选择 3，内部零概率区间与末尾零概率项均不能被选中。使用 C_i≥u 的错误版本会在这些明确边界上失败。\\\\n\\\\n连续均匀 u 落入区间 i 的概率等于区间长度 p_i，给出逆变换的分布依据。实际 RNG 只有有限离散输出，边界可能有正概率，因此不能用“相等事件概率为零”忽略比较符号。浮点累计还可能因归一化或舍入留下覆盖缺口，应预先声明数值策略并检查；无条件返回最后一项可能把末尾零概率项变成可选项。CDF 预处理为 O(V)，线性查找 O(V)；保留累计数组后可用寻找首个严格大于 u 的二分查找，单次 O(log V)，额外驻留 O(V)。重复累计值仍按同一严格边界处理。\\\\n\\\\n固定 seed 的一条文本只支持特定随机轨迹回归。频率检查需预先声明样本数、统计量、阈值和停止规则，例如总变差 0.5Σi|c_i/n−p_i|；其阈值与样本数和任务风险有关。置信区间或拟合检验还依赖独立性、平稳性及多重比较条件。确定性网格枚举能核对小分布的边界映射，不能冒充随机样本的统计检验。投机或拒绝采样还需证明接受与修正规则保持目标分布，单条输出相同不足以证明。\\\\n\\\\n数值容差、分布保持与任务质量分别判定。ASR 词错误率、分类准确率、检索排序、检测定位、图像或语音质量使用各自单位、保留集和失败规则。开发样例用于选择与定位，最终保留样例覆盖未参与选择的输入分层和状态时序。\\\\n\\\\n## 请求结果与终止记录的身份算法\\\\n\\\\n预期内容正确并不意味着结果属于当前尝试。设 A 当前被授权的结果身份为 (A,2,a,8)，值为 17；旧结果 (A,1,a,8,17) 仅改变尝试代次，仍必须拒绝。结果 (A,2,a,7,17) 仅改变槽代次，也必须拒绝。结果值完全相同，说明内容比较不能代替代次比较。\\\\n\\\\n一个有限检查可以冻结表 E[r]=(g,s,e,value,status)，其中每个 r 在本次检查范围内只有一个被授权尝试、一个指定结果槽以及一个应有结果和终止记录。E 从输入计划和授权快照独立声明，不从实际结果或终止记录生成。若生产任务允许同请求多个分支、多槽结果、取消后无结果或多个历史尝试，应把这些义务显式展开；不能直接套用这个单结果模型。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 CheckIdentity(E,Results,Terminals)\\\\n输入：独立冻结的非空 E；完整导出的结果与业务终止记录\\\\n输出：缺失、额外、重复、身份、内容与终止状态问题\\\\n1 分别建立结果账与终止账；两个账均以 r 定位本次义务\\\\n2 对两个账中的每条记录：\\\\n    若 r 不在 E：记录额外记录\\\\n    若同一账已出现 r：记录重复；不能以后一个覆盖前一个\\\\n    若 r 在 E：逐字段核对 g、s、e 与 E[r] 相同\\\\n3 对每个 E[r]：\\\\n    要求结果与终止账各恰好有一条对应记录\\\\n    结果内容必须等于 E[r].value\\\\n    终止状态必须等于 E[r].status，不能仅检查属于某个状态枚举\\\\n4 返回具体字段、预期值和实际值；任一问题均不能汇总为通过\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\nr 定位义务不代表忽略代次；g、s、e 必须分别比较。相反，若仅用观测的完整身份键建表，却不与授权 E 比较，旧结果仍可能被错误接受为另一个合法实例。两个账也必须各自对 E 核对，不能让错误结果与错误终止记录互相证明。\\\\n\\\\n完整日志范围内，预期 A=17、B=99，却返回 A=17、B=17，应拒绝 B 的内容；只保留 A 会产生缺失，重复 A 不能抵消缺失 B。导出链不完整时，缺失检查点是 UNKNOWN；随章脚本采用完整合成记录的前提，因而能明确拒绝缺失、重复和额外记录。真实运行需先证明相应日志覆盖。\\\\n\\\\n## 服务协议与共享取消组合\\\\n\\\\n协议 oracle 把响应看作有身份的事件序列。一个明确的普通流式合同可以要求：一个 start 先于 data；data 序号从 0 连续递增；恰好一个业务终止；终止后不再提交内容；按序拼接内容等于终止合同允许的内容；usage 与外部提交至多一次。这是应用合同，不能把一个简化状态机称为完整 ASGI、WebSocket、stop string 或背压实现。\\\\n\\\\nASGI 固定文档允许断开通知与发送失败存在竞争，旧版本也不保证关闭连接上的 send 一定报错。因此不要求 http.disconnect 与发送异常固定先后。send 返回只支持内容已进入服务器发送缓冲的相应语义，不证明客户端消费，也不能统一推导应用借用缓冲已经不再被读取。业务终态、设备排空、发送访问结束和远端消费分别记录。\\\\n\\\\n沿 A/B 共享前缀、A 取消和私有槽复用展开一条轨迹。P 是共享页，a 是 A 的私有槽，初始分配代次为 7；B 的 kernel 读取 P，A 的 DMA 使用 a。为便于核对，下表暂不设置缓存保留策略与隔离原因。\\\\n\\\\n| 时刻与事件 | P 的逻辑拥有者 / 未结束访问 | a 的逻辑拥有者 / 未结束访问 | 互斥容量类别与提交资格 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 登记访问后启动 | {A,B} / {B-kernel} | {A} / {A-DMA} | P、a 各计一次 Inflight；票据先于启动登记 |\\\\n| A 业务取消 | {B} / {B-kernel} | 空 / {A-DMA} | 两者仍为 Inflight；撤销 A 新输出资格，保留两项执行责任 |\\\\n| B-kernel 结束，B 仍继续 | {B} / 空 | 空 / {A-DMA} | P 转 Active；a 仍为 Inflight，不能交给 C |\\\\n| A-DMA 最后访问结束 | {B} / 空 | 空 / 空 | a 关闭旧生命期后转 Free；A 的业务终态不改变 |\\\\n| C 取得 a，代次推进至 8 | {B} / 空 | {C} / 空 | a 转 Active，初始化本代数据后才能发布给消费者 |\\\\n| A 的旧业务结果或重复完成晚到 | {B} / 空 | {C} / 当前代责任 | 旧 (A,g,a,7) 无提交权；旧已结算票据不能删除 C 的责任 |\\\\n| B、C 最后使用结束并释放拥有权 | 空 / 空 | 空 / 空 | 关闭取得旧对象的新资格后归 Free；若 P 被策略保留，则转 Retained |\\\\n\\\\n若 A-DMA 的完成证据缺失，a 进入 Quarantined，同时继续保存 A-DMA 责任；超时不能代替完成。业务取消可以先发生，资源责任在后续真实结束证据到达时结算。若每个页占 b 字节，A 取消后两个页仍有访问，暂时不可复用容量为 2b；不能因为仅剩 B 一个业务拥有者就只记 b。共享 P 的容量始终只有 b，不按 A/B 引用数倍增。\\\\n\\\\n参考分别从 A、B、C 的逻辑输入重建，检查 B 历史未被取消污染、C 未接收 A 的迟到结果、P 未被提前回收、a 未在旧访问结束前复用。身份错误、共享引用错误和完成错误具有不同见证。仅比较 B/C 最终文本可能漏掉迟到写入；仅检查最终全部空闲可能把提前回收也误判为成功。\\\\n\\\\n## 从正交责任生成互斥资源分区\\\\n\\\\n先固定容量统计域与物理对象粒度。Total 是本域内不重叠的物理单位 s；别名先归并到同一单位，或证明字节范围互不重叠。不同大小单位使用容量 b_s，不能只比较对象数量。每个单位保存当前分配代次 e，容量只计 s 一次，票据仍绑定 (s,e)。预留池容量与池内对象不能重复相加，虚拟地址预留也不自动等于物理驻留。\\\\n\\\\n对每个物理单位记录以下正交字段：\\\\n\\\\n- L：业务或模型版本的逻辑拥有者；共享页可同时有多个拥有者。\\\\n- U：已取得启动资格、尚未证明最后访问结束的执行责任，包括 kernel、DMA、图重放和外部读者。\\\\n- O：已取得输出读取权、尚未结束的消费者。\\\\n- B：长期地址或其他绑定责任。\\\\n- H：预留、未完成初始化或尚未取得启动资格但仍需保留对象的计划责任。\\\\n- K：具有具体策略与容量解释的保留根，例如缓存目录；它不等于请求拥有者 L。\\\\n- Q：隔离原因及逐项解除条件。\\\\n- closed：旧生命期已关闭新的取得资格；已有拥有者的合法使用仍按串行状态规则登记。\\\\n\\\\n这里把请求拥有权与缓存保留根分开，是为了说明归类；实际实现可以用带类型的统一责任表。不能把缓存目录既作为 L 又额外计一份物理容量。\\\\n\\\\n采用以下优先级，得到唯一类别：有 Q 则 Quarantined；否则有 U 或 O 则 Inflight；否则有 L、B、H 或尚未关闭取得资格则 Active；否则有 K 则 Retained；剩余为 Free。类别只用于容量投影，不删除其他字段。于是\\\\n\\\\nTotal = Free ⊎ Active ⊎ Inflight ⊎ Retained ⊎ Quarantined，\\\\n\\\\nΣs∈Total b_s = Σ各类别 Σs∈类别 b_s。\\\\n\\\\nA/B 共同拥有且 B 正在读取 P 时，P 只计入 Inflight，L_P={A,B} 与 U_P={B-kernel} 都保留；不是同时放入 Active，也不是为了互斥而删掉在途责任。隔离页即使仍有拥有者和 DMA，也只归 Quarantined，具体阻塞仍由 L、U、O、B、H、Q 解释。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 ClassifyPhysicalSnapshot(Total,Raw)\\\\n输入：同一一致性边界上的物理单位全集及完整正交状态\\\\n输出：五个互斥容量列表和保留原字段的诊断快照\\\\n1 初始化五个列表为空；核对每个 s 恰好有一份 Raw[s]\\\\n2 对每个 s：\\\\n    若 Q[s] 非空：类别←Quarantined\\\\n    否则若 U[s] 或 O[s] 非空：类别←Inflight\\\\n    否则若 L[s]、B[s]、H[s] 任一非空，或 closed[s]=false：类别←Active\\\\n    否则若 K[s] 非空：类别←Retained\\\\n    否则：类别←Free\\\\n    把 s 加入唯一类别；保留所有责任字段及代次\\\\n3 核对列表内外均无重复、并集等于 Total、容量和相等\\\\n4 用独立操作票据账核对 Raw 中 U/O 的完整性和 (s,e) 身份\\\\n5 返回分区与阻塞责任；仅分区成立不等于已排空\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n一个错误分类器可能把 P 仅放 Active，此时并集与唯一性均成立，却违反语义优先级。因此检查需要同时验证“分区是否完整互斥”与“类别是否由真实责任得到”。另一个错误观测器可能删掉 U 后将 P 放 Active；如果没有独立的启动/完成票据账，任何只读这个残缺快照的分区算法都无法恢复丢失事实。受控逻辑实验可用预先声明的票据作为独立参考，真实系统则需要对应域的完整登记与完成证据。\\\\n\\\\n责任登记、关闭生命期与生成快照需要同一串行状态域，或等价的锁、原子事务与一致性快照。分别读取两个时刻的 L 和 U，可能制造不存在的 Free 状态。完成只结算匹配 (r,g,s,e,uid) 的责任；重复旧通知不能递减另一个使用者，未知通知也不能清空当前代。\\\\n\\\\n对本章的可排空请求池，静止态要求 U、O、Q 为空且无 Active；Free 等于 Total 减去有解释的 Retained。服务级长期权重、图绑定等若属于统计域，应与预先声明的存活基线比较，不能要求仍在服务的权重全部释放。RSS 不下降时，要区分分配器可复用保留、策略缓存和不可达泄漏；最终归类与容量解释比单一进程指标更有判别力。\\\\n\\\\n## 检查流程与条件化成本\\\\n\\\\n检查先冻结要求，再判断观测，最后验证检查器的辨别力。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 ValidateObligations(C,Oracle,Expected,Observed,Terminals,Resources)\\\\n输入：任务与 oracle 契约、独立预期义务、观测与终止、资源证据\\\\n输出：逐实例判定、失败见证、缺口和明确覆盖范围\\\\n1 核对版本、输入、单位与参考合法域；已知不相容记 INVALID\\\\n2 保留预先声明的全部义务；未采集或被前序失败阻断的义务不删除\\\\n3 核对结果、终止与资源票据身份；按对应契约检查重复、缺失和额外记录\\\\n4 对证据充分且前提相容的实例执行函数、变形、概率或协议关系\\\\n5 从完整正交责任生成并验证资源分区；单独判断排空与允许基线\\\\n6 把已知错误输入或错误算法送入实际比较器，要求产生对应失败见证\\\\n7 负对照未检出则撤回相应检查器资格；不能输出该维度的引擎通过\\\\n8 仅当义务非空、全部完成有效判定且均通过，汇总本次通过\\\\n  其他情况保留 FAIL、UNKNOWN、INVALID 与具体未覆盖范围\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n设序列长度 T、隐藏维 d、层数 L、词表 V。每个生成位置都重做长度 t 的完整稠密 prefill，attention 主项累计 Σt²d=O(T³d)；仅对最后一个 query 使用合法独立历史，主项累计 O(T²d)，但各层历史 K/V 仍须合法产生。其他投影和 MLP 成本要另计；减少 attention 主项不自动给出完整模型加速。\\\\n\\\\n全部层 hidden 的观察驻留为 O(LTd)，逐层只保留一对为 O(Td)。设 T=2048、d=4096、L=32，FP32 一份 hidden 为 32 MiB，一对为 64 MiB，32 层全部配对为 2 GiB；不含 Q/K/V、权重和缓存。V=32000 时全量 logits 为 250 MiB，末行约 125 KiB。只观察末行减少采集与传输，却没有检查未导出的层、位置和状态。\\\\n\\\\n身份、协议与资源元数据检查的平均时间可分别随记录数、内容字节与责任条目数线性增长；哈希账需要相应驻留，若排序输出诊断还要支付排序成本。协议内容分块保存后统一拼接，可避免每次追加复制整个已收内容。保存所有历史快照的驻留随时间增长，可用增量账与选定检查点，但必须保留重建所需事件和覆盖范围。\\\\n\\\\n六类成本应同时列账：计算包括影子前向、独立整数参考、CDF 和比较；访存包括被比较张量与元数据遍历；通信包括设备到主机快照和跨设备摘要；准备包括模型加载、前处理、独立页表与量化元数据构造；同步包括主机读取设备结果、完成等待和一致性快照；驻留包括影子权重、激活、观测缓冲、票据账及在途采集。一次一个设备标量的读取可能引入很多同步，不能只按几个字节估价。\\\\n\\\\n端到端时间沿依赖关键路径与共享资源计算，不能把可重叠阶段的耗时全部相加，也不能假定完全重叠。诊断同步、复制与影子参考会扰动执行，甚至掩盖竞态；正常性能运行与诊断运行分别计时。逻辑容量算例不构成设备事务量或实测时延。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n| 条件变化 | 保留的关系 | 调整或放弃的依据 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 长度、页长或 chunk 改变 | 输入历史、全局位置和可见集合 | 重算参考与采集成本；不能为容量静默截短任务 |\\\\n| dtype、量化格式或尺度改变 | 原模型质量基线与独立代数 | 重建同制品参考及舍入契约；旧码不可任意配新尺度 |\\\\n| batch、物理页与完成顺序改变 | 请求归属、对象身份和责任守恒 | 核对逆映射及浮点重排；增加受控时序 |\\\\n| 前缀缓存、迁移或驱逐改变 | 内容、模型与表示身份 | 身份不相容则放弃缓存等价，改查重建和质量 |\\\\n| 重试或部分输出合同改变 | 逻辑任务身份与提交权限 | 显式展开各尝试、允许内容和终止义务，不按返回结果删样本 |\\\\n| RNG、设备或归约树改变 | 数学函数、支持集和任务质量 | 重建随机流与数值路径；放弃无依据的跨平台逐位要求 |\\\\n| 资源池或保留策略改变 | 唯一物理容量与责任完整性 | 重定统计域、策略保留根与静止基线，不能沿用旧 RSS 阈值 |\\\\n| 协议版本与连接行为改变 | 业务终态和外部提交语义 | 重核发送、断开与借用缓冲边界，不要求固定竞争顺序 |\\\\n\\\\n诊断需要竞争解释与可否定预测。\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分实验与反证后的修正 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 常规采样正常，精确边界错 | 非严格 CDF 比较、零概率处理或 RNG 映射 | 用精确有理数固定 u=累计边界及零概率首项；数值无舍入仍错则修选择规则 |\\\\n| 共享页被报重复占用 | 真正重复账或将拥有权与执行责任混作容量类别 | 固定 L={A,B}、U={B-kernel}；应仅计一次 Inflight，仍能列出两个拥有者 |\\\\n| 分区互斥却提前回收 | 启动票据遗漏、错误完成结算或快照不一致 | 保持物理集合不变，独立核对启动/完成账；删 U 后不能靠并集通过掩盖缺失 |\\\\n| 同值旧结果被接受 | 只比较内容、仅按 rid 去重或终止账未校验代次 | 固定内容，仅分别改变结果与终止的 g、s、e；每个错误字段都应被实际比较器拒绝 |\\\\n| 仅跨页或 chunk 失败 | 页映射、位置重置、尾部可见性或尺度 | 保持逻辑输入，分别改页排列与 chunk；随物理页走时查映射，随 chunk 走时查位置推进 |\\\\n| token 改变而 logits 接近 | 小 margin、processor 或选择规则变化 | 比较处理前后分布并计算 margin；大于 2ε 仍改变时不能仅归因于该误差界内的舍入 |\\\\n| 取消后 RSS 不下降 | 分配器保留、缓存根、未结束访问或真实泄漏 | 核对互斥容量、正交责任和结束证据；无完成证明的页继续隔离 |\\\\n| 同 seed 文本不同 | RNG 消费顺序、非确定性归约或身份串用 | 固定逐请求随机数重放同一快照；随机数固定后仍失败则继续检查数值与状态 |\\\\n| 局部整数参考一致但质量下降 | 近似损失、校准漂移或跨层组合 | 分别恢复权重、KV 与敏感层精度；只有相应干预有效才收窄归因 |\\\\n\\\\n反证应修改判断。提高参考精度后仍有固定漏项，应转向索引和覆盖；删除诊断同步后竞态重现，不能把有同步的通过当作正常路径安全证明。负对照应尽量只改变所研究维度，防止同时破坏全部格式而无法知道哪个规则生效。\\\\n\\\\n## 会话失败范围与检查器修复\\\\n\\\\n多轮会话的后续输入可能依赖前序有效输出。前一轮失败后的未执行请求属于缺失或被阻断，不能从预先计划的会话集合删除，也不能计为通过。分别报告计划逻辑轮次、实际发起、接纳、拒绝、完成、取消、超时与质量失败。请求级分母由任务预先声明；会话成功需要全部必要依赖完成，请求级条件成功率不能替代会话成功率。\\\\n\\\\n用户要求完整历史、精确内容或完整候选集合时，测试驱动不能为了可运行而截短历史、忽略错误请求或放松质量定义。可以选择小规模独立参考，但应明确它缩小了证据范围，原任务要求并未因此改变。\\\\n\\\\n发现比较器缺陷后，定位受影响规则、检查版本和历史结论。原始输入、输出、身份与事件足够时，可用修订后的检查器重新分析并保留新旧身份；缺少必要字段时，需重跑对应路径。修复身份比较器恢复了拒绝旧结果的能力，不能自动证明过去候选的输出从未串代。也不应把与缺陷无关的全部证据笼统清零。\\\\n\\\\n## 随章检查及未验证范围\\\\n\\\\n随章文件 tools/check_k_tools_006_full.py 是确定性、离线、只读的 Python 标准库检查。它具有独立给定的身份预期、CDF 边界表、全局位置加权参考、协议固定内容与序号规则，以及资源手工期望分区和独立票据账。负对照穿过实际比较器，包括非严格 CDF、同内容旧代次、错误槽、终止身份串代、共享页错误分类、遗漏在途责任和重复物理计数。\\\\n\\\\n身份模型检查 rid、attempt 对应 g、slot 对应 s、epoch 对应 e，以及结果值和终止状态；结果与终止各自对冻结预期核对。模型假定每个请求在该批只有一个授权的成功结果和一个指定结果槽。它没有实现分支 ID、逻辑 token 位置 t、模型/表示版本 v、逐 chunk 请求映射、生产提交权限或任意多槽请求。资源票据额外携带 (r,g,s,e,uid)，但仅验证有限快照中的匹配与完整性，没有实现真实设备完成适配器。\\\\n\\\\n资源检查覆盖共享拥有者与在途访问同时存在、取消后仍在途、访问结束后转 Active、最终释放与策略保留，以及 Quarantined 优先归类；它不证明实际登记链没有漏掉未观测访问。协议检查仅为单条合成流的 extracted-character range 0:4000]\\\\n# K-SYS-010：系统设计推导：把模型、缓存、执行与目标组合起来\\\\n\\\\n专家指导的产物不是一组彼此独立的优化提示，而是一条从任务条件到系统结构的可反驳推导链：状态模型、资源模型、候选设计、成本下界、证据状态和能区分竞争解释的实验。候选必须满足函数、身份、资源和完成条件，才有资格进入性能比较。下界通过只表示尚未被排除；上界未通过只表示尚未证明达标。两者都不能直接替代实际结果。\\\\n\\\\n## 统一问题表述：从条件到设计证书\\\\n\\\\n把设计条件写成 C＝(F,W,H,N,Q,S,E)。F 是模型函数、参数、位置规则、数值语义和必需状态；W 是到达过程、输入输出长度、前缀复用和会话依赖；H 是处理器、内存层级、互连、存储与拓扑；N 是运行时、编译器、驱动和可用执行路径；Q 是质量与数值容差；S 是首内容、逐 token、完成时间、吞吐、拒绝与公平目标；E 是已有来源事实、推导和测量及其作用域。设计变量 d 可以包含状态布局、缓存身份、调度粒度、执行后端、并行策略、阶段划分、队列和准入。\\\\n\\\\n输出不是单一总分，而是对每个条件格 k 和候选 d 给出设计证书：合法性、状态转移、各资源成本、证据支持的上下界、质量状态、排除理由，以及下一步区分实验。条件格是 F、W、H、N 的有限代表区域，例如模型版本、批大小、历史长度与共享或独立内存域的组合。格内连续变化的量仍须保留范围；中心点的结果不能自动覆盖整个格。\\\\n\\\\n设请求 r 的已知 token 数为 nᵣ，已提交且各必要层完整、可复用的 KV 终点为 cᵣ，满足 0≤cᵣ≤nᵣ。已生成文本不等于对应 KV 已计算；物理页已提交也不等于所有异步读者已经结束。系统在时刻 t 的驻留量为\\\\n\\\\nM(t)＝W_phys(t)＋Σ_unique P_state(t)＋A_work(t)＋I_flight(t)＋Q_queued(t)，\\\\n\\\\n其中 W_phys 是各物理副本的权重，P_state 是按存储域去重的状态页，A_work 是工作区，I_flight 是在途传输或暂定写，Q_queued 是消费者尚未释放的输出缓冲。同一物理 backing 在这些项间不重复计数。容量条件是 max_t M(t)≤M_cap；各项各自峰值之和只是保守上界，未必能在同一时刻达到。\\\\n\\\\n设计还必须固定比较的时间量 θ。它可以是某次固定执行的完成时间、预先指定有限回放的最大 ITL，或某个到达分布下的总体平均值、p99。它们是不同对象。下界、上界、观测和目标只有指向相同 θ，或存在明确的蕴含关系时，才能共同裁决候选。\\\\n\\\\n## 设计对象、合法性与证据状态\\\\n\\\\n合法性至少包含四层。函数合法性要求候选实现任务规定的模型函数、mask、位置、归一化和输出；数值合法性要求 dtype、累加、缩放、舍入和容差契约相容；设备语义要求布局、指令、可见性和完成事件支持所选路径；身份与并发合法性要求请求、版本、页、adapter、输出和迟到通知不会串用。任何一层失败都不能用平均更快抵消。允许近似的任务可以比较不同表示或求解轨迹，但必须把相应质量门槛写入 Q。\\\\n\\\\n普通稠密 GQA decoder 每 token 全层 KV 字节为\\\\n\\\\nb_KV＝2·L·H_kv·d_h·s，\\\\n\\\\nL 是层数，H_kv 是 KV head 数，d_h 是每 head 维数，s 是每元素字节。MLA 的持久 latent 不同，可按 L·(d_c＋d_Rh)·s 计算每 token 缓存主项。专家权重、临时分组激活、通信区与输出头另列。公式只描述声明的状态表示，不证明后端已选择相应 kernel。\\\\n\\\\n逻辑共享不等于物理共享，物理共享也不等于每次读取只发生一次。多个请求映射到同一物理前缀页时，容量账计一次；没有跨请求广播、片上驻留或其他复用契约时，各请求 attention 仍须取得自身可见历史，流量账不能直接去重。将共享页从流量中无证据扣除会低估带宽时间；把每次逻辑读取都当成新物理页又会高估容量。\\\\n\\\\n证书分别保存时间结论、质量状态与过期证据。下表的标签是主决策，原始证据及其他轴不因选择一个主标签而丢失。\\\\n\\\\n| 标签 | 含义与处理 | 不能推出 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| `ILLEGAL_LEGALITY` | 已确认硬合法条件失败；排除当前候选与条件格的组合 | 修改表示或算法后的新候选也非法 |\\\\n| `ILLEGAL_CAPACITY` | 已确认该执行计划必需的峰值驻留超过容量 | 仅因一个宽松容量上界超预算就证明不可容纳 |\\\\n| `EXCLUDED_LOWER_BOUND` | 有效时间下界超过目标，且未发现同作用域矛盾证据 | 其他条件格也应排除 |\\\\n| `EXCLUDED_MEASURED` | 相应作用域的直接观测或获准统计证据支持时间失败 | 任意保守上界超过目标即可排除 |\\\\n| `EXCLUDED_QUALITY` | 同作用域质量证据判定失败；当前组合不能满足联合目标 | 提升速度能抵消质量失败 |\\\\n| `LOWER_BOUND_SURVIVOR` | 当前未证明失败，也未证明时间与质量全部通过；保留开放候选 | 已满足 SLO |\\\\n| `QUALITY_PENDING` | 时间已获支持通过，质量未知或质量证据过期；保留但不计为合格方案 | 可以省略质量评估 |\\\\n| `VERIFIED` | 同作用域时间与质量均按声明证据口径通过 | 其他形状、设备、负载或总体分位数也通过 |\\\\n| `EVIDENCE_STALE` | 尚开放，且存在不适用的时间或质量证据；记录失配字段 | 证据本身错误，或有效的其他排除证据失效 |\\\\n| `INCONSISTENT` | 对同一时间量的有效约束无共同解；转诊断并暂停相互矛盾证据的裁决效力 | 目标实现一定不可行 |\\\\n\\\\n质量采用 `pass`、`fail`、`unknown` 三态。未评估、区间不能裁决、任务分布改变或证据作用域失配都按 `unknown`；不能把没有发现质量错误解释为 `pass`。同作用域 `fail` 排除当前候选，`unknown` 保留候选但禁止 `VERIFIED`。质量评估依据可以是任务认可的独立数值参考、等价性论证或任务评估，具体范围必须记录。离线分类检查只消费这些状态，不生成真实模型质量结论。\\\\n\\\\n容量也要区分证明方向：精确计划峰值或必要驻留下界超容量可以排除；保守容量上界超过容量只说明该上界不能证明容纳。资源尚无法裁决时保留为资源待确认的开放候选。随章分类函数的布尔容量参数限定为容量已决的情况，不模拟这个未决阶段。\\\\n\\\\n## 上界、观测与统计口径怎样进入决策\\\\n\\\\n对固定候选与条件格，设目标为 θ≤τ，且已有有效下界 L。时间证据分三类。\\\\n\\\\n- 保守上界 U 声明 θ≤U。U≤τ 足以支持时间通过；U>τ 不说明 θ>τ。\\\\n- 直接观测 y 可以精确描述预先指定的有限执行或有限回放统计量，此时对那个有限对象有 θ=y。它不自动描述未来总体。\\\\n- 对总体均值或分位数的统计证据，应保留估计量、实验单位、区间 [a,b]、置信口径及方法假设。按预先声明的统计决策规则，b≤τ 支持通过，a>τ 支持失败，跨阈值则开放。点估计或样本最大值不能擅自变成总体硬上界。\\\\n\\\\n作用域至少核对模型及制品、表示和布局、backend、dtype、batch 与长度、缓存条件、资源域与并发、到达和拒绝口径、计时起止、目标统计量及其人群。计时误差也要进入观测区间。将多个统计区间共同使用前，须说明联合覆盖或决策规则；分别名义 95% 的区间不能无说明地拼成一个确定证书。[性能实验](../tools/statistical-experiments.md)进一步区分运行、请求与环境重复。\\\\n\\\\n把适用证据与下界相交，得到\\\\n\\\\nL*＝max(L, 所有适用观测区间的下端)，\\\\n\\\\nU*＝min(所有适用保守上界及观测区间的上端)，\\\\n\\\\n没有上端证据时 U*＝＋∞。若 L*>U*，先进入 `INCONSISTENT`，即使 L 已超过目标也不能提前按它排除。这里的矛盾表示各前提或区间不能同时采用；对于统计区间，它还可能暴露覆盖失败或方法不适用，不能立即断言硬件违反物理定律。\\\\n\\\\n宽松上界的反例是 L＝39.0625 ms、U＝80 ms、τ＝60 ms。实际值可以为 50 ms，同时满足 L≤50≤U 和目标；仅凭这组界必须保留候选。反过来，若已有同作用域有效上界 55 ms，而声明下界为 70 ms、目标为 60 ms，先排除会错删一个可能通过的方案。正确动作是保存冲突，检查单位、资源能力、缓存前提和计时边界，修正证据后重新分类。\\\\n\\\\n若时间上界 55 ms 通过目标 60 ms，但质量为 `fail`，结果是 `EXCLUDED_QUALITY`；质量为 `unknown` 时是 `QUALITY_PENDING`；只有质量为有效 `pass` 才能成为 `VERIFIED`。这三个分支不要求离线检查执行真实模型评估。\\\\n\\\\n## 完整推导算法：候选、条件格与证据更新\\\\n\\\\n以下算法串联条件、合法性、容量、下界、观测、质量与下一实验。候选族可以来自参数化搜索、已有实现或人工设计。已有测量可以先于解析推导取得，不要求研发按伪代码的论证顺序施工。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 SYNTHESIZE(C,D,budget)\\\\n输入：C=(F,W,H,N,Q,S,E)；候选族 D；实验预算\\\\n输出：逐格设计证书、保留候选与下一实验，或明确的空集原因\\\\n\\\\n1 归一化单位、逻辑轴、目标统计量和时间窗；将条件划分为有限格 K\\\\n  若 K 为空，报告缺少目标条件；若 D 为空，报告没有候选\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n[EXCERPT extracted-character range 8000:8844]\\\\natch 需同时计算路径、排队、偏斜与接收端容量。若做 prefill/decode 分离，还需计状态传输、分片转换和完整提交。较小 KV 不等于网络免费，也不意味着专家热点解决。\\\\n\\\\n区分实验可以固定模型和请求，只改变 EP 度数，记录每链路字节、专家最大负载及尾延迟；固定 EP、只改变 TP，记录本地分片与归约时间；固定并行计划、改变路由或共享前缀，观察队列和流量是否按预测变化。训练时的路由均衡目标不保证每次推理严格均衡。若实际干预同时改变副本、路由和 batch，需要拆开或记录这些中介变化，不能用一个平均吞吐裁决所有解释。\\\\n\\\\n## 场景四：静态编译平台上的混合长度任务\\\\n\\\\n模型函数固定而服务形状变化时，可按 prompt、query、context 和 batch 的联合分布选择有限桶。设备保留 KV，控制面推进真实长度；越界走明确回退、较粗桶或拒绝，不能静默截断。编译准备、executable、workspace 和图池驻留共同进入启动与容量预算。\\\\n\\\\n前缀命中改变待算 query 分布，连续批改变 batch 分布，投机改变验证长度分布。桶选择应在这些机制组合后的 workload 上推导。命中后 query 变短、host 固定成本上升时，大 decode 桶未必优于专门小桶；长请求比例上升后，粗桶的 padding 和 KV 驻留又会改变比较。\\\\n\\\\n固定 NxD Inference 文档的前缀缓存路径先 gather 块 KV，再转换到 flat 布局计算，最后 scatter 回去；这说明支持共享状态不等于直接使用 PagedAttention。布局转换的准备、读取、写入与驻留要进入该候选，不能把另一 backend 的流量模型直接移植过来。\\\\n\\\\n## 组合轨迹：CPU 多请求生成的完整推导\\\\n\\\\n以下参数全部是可复算设定，不是目标机器或模型实测。任务是固定版本稠密 GQA decoder 文本生成，质量由独立固定前缀 forward 与任务评估判定。8 个\\\\n\\\\n[EXCERPT extracted-character range 12000:19298]\\\\n 需要一起检验的关系 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| C01 CPU 多请求生成 | 本章 CPU 场景 | 权重/KV 流量、线程与 prefill 时间片、开放到达和 ITL |\\\\n| C02 单 GPU 交互 | [CUDA 平台](../hardware/cuda-execution.md) | 容量、带宽、内核与主机间隙、准入和输出 |\\\\n| C03 长上下文高复用 | [前缀缓存](../algorithms/prefix-cache-identity.md) | 物理共享容量、逻辑读取、路由与长尾 |\\\\n| C04 显存不足与三级存储 | 各自输入、状态与任务指标；五种契约分别验证 |\\\\n\\\\n场景可以交叉：RAG 调用 embedding、检索、重排与生成，多模态服务同时需要多模型放置和低延迟音频。组合时重新计算共同资源与状态，不能把各场景的独占带宽或独立质量结果直接相加。\\\\n\\\\n## 实例方案要能落到服务和平台\\\\n\\\\n多节点任务的执行组可能受 [集群放置](../workloads/cluster-resource-placement.md)拓扑与故障余量影响；共享制品、缓存和提交记录引入 [存储服务](storage-services.md)的相应语义。它们由候选实现还是环境提供，取决于任务；单机和离线引擎不因此自动增加功能要求。[部署环境](deployment-environment.md)说明真实配额、设备和版本，进程存活、文件存在或空闲卡数各自只提供局部信息。\\\\n\\\\n这些示例通过任务条件、状态、计算、流量、容量、交互与观测解释方案。其他设计可以采用不同表示和组织；没有恢复或请求排队的任务不需要补造对应模块。已有优化可以按需求采用、重组或省略，结论取决于实际前提和证据。\\\\n\\\\n## 设计例子的适用范围与未列路径\\\\n\\\\n上述场景不穷尽架构或设计变量。Task 决定交付的函数、质量、性能与资源边界；一个例子的调度器、状态池、阶段和验证顺序不会自动成为另一任务的要求。独立调度、整体编译、持久执行和其他组织方式应按实际结果判断。\\\\n\\\\n机制依赖与研发顺序不同。消费者需要有效输入，不等于工程上必须先冻结全部接口；可以用独立实验检查成本假设，再联合修正模型、表示、融合边界和调度。验证保留实际覆盖范围，最终按任务验收。\\\\n\\\\n候选可以扩展、组合或全部放弃。新方案没有现成章节或来源实现并不失格；改变表示、硬件能力或任务质量后，原先的排除前提也可能不再成立。阅读来源、符合例子步骤或获得状态标签本身不构成正确或更优的证据。\\\\n\\\\n## 布局改变后的完整成本与反转条件\\\\n\\\\n以下是设定反例。原路径在输入已满足布局时计算 1.0 ms，新 kernel 计算 0.6 ms，但需要 0.5 ms 输入转换；两者串行且不能隐藏时，一次执行为 1.1 ms。同一合法转换结果可复用 R 次时，新路径总成本为 0.5＋0.6R ms，原路径为 R ms，严格获益要求 R>1.25；R＝2 时为 1.7 对 2.0 ms。\\\\n\\\\n上游直接产生目标布局、融合转换与计算或改变状态表示，都会改变成本项。输入每次改变则复用前提失效；转换与其他消费者争用带宽也要重算。该公式判断声明的候选，不排除能改变其前提的新设计。准备时间的保守上界超过收益预算时，同样不能冒充实际一定更慢的证据。\\\\n\\\\n## 区分实验、反证与修正\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分干预与预测 | 反证后的修正 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 命中率上升但队列更长 | 亲和集中；短 query 主机成本；保留页挤占容量 | 控制实际命中边界后改路由；固定命中改 query；固定计算增加容量 | 按真正改变结果的干预修路由、准备或保留策略 |\\\\n| batch 增大后 token/s 上升而 ITL 超标 | 权重摊薄；轮转等待；prefill 干扰 | 固定历史改变 batch，分记每轮与请求等待；单独开关分块 | 收窄 batch、准入或阶段组织，不把总吞吐当 SLO |\\\\n| 两副本没有加速 | 共享带宽；权重复制；路由集中；锁或输出竞争 | 同流量比较共享域与独立域，记录带宽、份额与等待 | 独立域改善才支持带宽解释，否则检查其余路径 |\\\\n| 位宽下降而时间不降 | 解包、转换、归约、fallback；主机准备；事务未降 | 固定形状与质量门槛，分别改变位宽、kernel 与线程，核对实际路径 | 撤回不受观察支持的带宽归因，数值与质量另验 |\\\\n| 图重放仍有主机间隙 | 捕获不完整；缓冲更新；输入等待 | 固定请求改变捕获边界，分记 plan/replay，预填输入 | 准备增长则修准备，仍排队则查准入与供给 |\\\\n| 上界 80 ms 超目标 60 ms | 上界宽松；实际确实超标 | 取得同作用域观测或收紧上界；50 ms 的合法结果能反驳“上界超标即失败” | 保留开放候选，只有有效失败观测或下界才支持排除 |\\\\n| 耗时证据通过但不能认定合格 | 质量失败；质量未知或过期 | 固定候选，用既定独立参考与任务评估裁决质量 | 失败排除当前组合，未知保留待验，均禁止 VERIFIED |\\\\n| 观测或上界低于声明下界 | 单位、计时窗、读取层级或缓存前提错误；统计方法失配 | 核对对象与起止，隔离阶段并使用独立计数或参考 | 先转 INCONSISTENT，修前提后重算，不先用矛盾下界删候选 |\\\\n\\\\n实验单位应是独立运行、条件格或预定配对区组，同一运行的相关 token 不自动独立。报告原始到达、完成、拒绝、超时和队列增长；不能只挑成功请求均值。一次干预同时改变 routing、缓存和 batch 时，需控制或报告这些变化。\\\\n\\\\n随章 `tools/check_k_sys_010_full.py` 是标准库、确定性、离线、只读的软件模型。它用独立物理 token 槽集合与逐请求读取枚举核对容量和流量，用有理数核对 CPU 设定算例，再以有限可能耗时集合检验分类。负对照实际执行错误分类分支，包括宽上界当失败、忽略质量、矛盾检查之前按下界排除和下界当通过；集合参考必须拒绝这些结果。检查还覆盖作用域失配、阈值相等、区间跨阈值和直接观测。\\\\n\\\\n该检查不产生统计区间，不证明输入证据真实或区间覆盖有效，不执行真实 forward、异步物理回收、CPU/GPU 性能或质量实验。分类枚举使用有限整数耗时域；另有明确的 39.0625 ms 有理数反例。目标平台的同步、事务、总体尾延迟和质量继续需要相应证据。\\\\n\\\\n## 从推导到 RSI 增量\\\\n\\\\n规划指出链条中最不确定的关系，执行实现对应机制，诊断核对预测与实际状态。进化把新认识写回受影响机制：补足成本、修正恢复条件或组合分支。成功不必产生新条目，更精确理解现有关系本身就是增量。\\\\n\\\\n写回记录对象身份、依赖边、单位、条件格和证据口径。例如共享页降低容量与降低每请求读取是不同命题；保守上界超过目标与实际失败也是不同命题。页表唯一化支持前者的容量关系，广播或片上复用才支持读取去重；同作用域失败观测或下界才支持排除。把局部实验时间差或一个宽松界直接写成通用机制，会把证据范围扩成它未证明的结论。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- ===\\\\nBERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for\\\\nLanguage Understanding\\\\nJacob Devlin\\\\nMing-Wei Chang\\\\nKenton Lee\\\\nKristina Toutanova\\\\nGoogle AI Language\\\\n{jacobdevlin,mingweichang,kentonl,kristout}@google.com\\\\nAbstract\\\\nWe introduce a new language representa-\\\\ntion model called BERT, which stands for\\\\nBidirectional Encoder Representations from\\\\nTransformers. Unlike recent language repre-\\\\nsentation models (Peters et al., 2018; Radford\\\\net al., 2018), BERT is designed to pre-train\\\\ndeep bidirectional representations by jointly\\\\nconditioning on both left and right context in\\\\nall layers. As a result, the pre-trained BERT\\\\nrepresentations can be ﬁne-tuned with just one\\\\nadditional output layer to create state-of-the-\\\\nart models for a wide range of tasks, such\\\\nas question answering and language inference,\\\\nwithout substantial task-speciﬁc architecture\\\\nmodiﬁcations.\\\\nBERT is conceptually simple and empirically\\\\npowerful.\\\\nIt obtains new state-of-the-art re-\\\\nsults on eleven natural language processing\\\\ntasks, including pushing the GLUE bench-\\\\nmark to 80.4% (7.6% absolute improvement),\\\\nMultiNLI accuracy to 86.7% (5.6% abso-\\\\nlute improvement) and the SQuAD v1.1 ques-\\\\ntion answering Test F1 to 93.2 (1.5 absolute\\\\nimprovement), outperforming human perfor-\\\\nmance by 2.0.\\\\n1\\\\nIntroduction\\\\nLanguage model pre-training has shown to be ef-\\\\nfective for improving many natural language pro-\\\\ncessing tasks (Dai and Le, 2015; Peters et al.,\\\\n2017, 2018; Radford et al., 2018; Howard and\\\\nRuder, 2018). These tasks include sentence-level\\\\ntasks such as natural language inference (Bow-\\\\nman et al., 2015; Williams et al., 2018) and para-\\\\nphrasing (Dolan and Brockett, 2005), which aim\\\\nto predict the relationships between sentences by\\\\nanalyzing them holistically, as well as token-level\\\\ntasks such as named entity recognition (Tjong\\\\nKim Sang and De Meulder, 2003) and SQuAD\\\\nquestion answering (Rajpurkar et al., 2016), where\\\\nmodels are required to produce ﬁne-grained output\\\\nat the token-level.\\\\nThere are two existing strategies for apply-\\\\ning pre-trained language representations to down-\\\\nstream tasks: feature-based and ﬁne-tuning. The\\\\nfeature-based approach, such as ELMo (Peters\\\\net al., 2018), uses tasks-speciﬁc architectures that\\\\ninclude the pre-trained representations as addi-\\\\ntional features. The ﬁne-tuning approach, such as\\\\nthe Generative Pre-trained Transformer (OpenAI\\\\nGPT) (Radford et al., 2018), introduces minimal\\\\ntask-speciﬁc parameters, and is trained on the\\\\ndownstream tasks by simply ﬁne-tuning the pre-\\\\ntrained parameters.\\\\nIn previous work, both ap-\\\\nproaches share the same objective function dur-\\\\ning pre-training, where they use unidirectional lan-\\\\nguage models to learn general language represen-\\\\ntations.\\\\nWe argue that current techniques severely re-\\\\nstrict the power of the pre-trained representations,\\\\nespecially for the ﬁne-tuning approaches. The ma-\\\\njor limitation is that standard language models are\\\\nunidirectional, and this limits the choice of archi-\\\\ntectures that can be used during pre-training. For\\\\nexample, in OpenAI GPT, the authors use a left-\\\\nto-right architecture, where every token can only\\\\nattended to previous tokens in the self-attention\\\\nlayers of the Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017).\\\\nSuch restrictions are sub-optimal for sentence-\\\\nlevel tasks, and could be devastating when ap-\\\\nplying ﬁne-tuning based approaches to token-level\\\\ntasks such as SQuAD question answering (Ra-\\\\njpurkar et al., 2016), where it is crucial to incor-\\\\nporate context from both directions.\\\\nIn this paper, we improve the ﬁne-tuning based\\\\napproaches by proposing BERT: Bidirectional\\\\nEncoder\\\\nRepresentations\\\\nfrom\\\\nTransformers.\\\\nBERT addresses the previously mentioned uni-\\\\ndirectional\\\\nconstraints\\\\nby\\\\nproposing\\\\na\\\\nnew\\\\npre-training objective:\\\\nthe “masked language\\\\narXiv:1810.04805v1  [cs.CL]  11 Oct 2018\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 2 ===\\\\nmodel” (MLM), inspired by the Cloze task (Tay-\\\\nlor, 1953). The masked language model randomly\\\\nmasks some of the tokens from the input, and the\\\\nobjective is to predict the original vocabulary id of\\\\nthe masked word based only on its context. Un-\\\\nlike left-to-right language model pre-training, the\\\\nMLM objective allows the representation to fuse\\\\nthe left and the right context, which allows us\\\\nto pre-train a deep bidirectional Transformer. In\\\\naddition to the masked language model, we also\\\\nintroduce a “next sentence prediction” task that\\\\njointly pre-trains text-pair representations.\\\\nThe contributions of our paper are as follows:\\\\n• We demonstrate the importance of bidirec-\\\\ntional pre-training for language representa-\\\\ntions. Unlike Radford et al. (2018), which\\\\nuses unidirectional language models for pre-\\\\ntraining, BERT uses masked language mod-\\\\nels to enable pre-trained deep bidirectional\\\\nrepresentations.\\\\nThis is also in contrast to\\\\nPeters et al. (2018), which uses a shallow\\\\nconcatenation of independently trained left-\\\\nto-right and right-to-left LMs.\\\\n• We show that pre-trained representations\\\\neliminate\\\\nthe\\\\nneeds\\\\nof\\\\nmany\\\\nheavily-\\\\nengineered task-speciﬁc architectures. BERT\\\\nis the ﬁrst ﬁne-tuning based representation\\\\nmodel that achieves state-of-the-art perfor-\\\\nmance on a large suite of sentence-level and\\\\ntoken-level tasks, outperforming many sys-\\\\ntems with task-speciﬁc architectures.\\\\n• BERT advances the state-of-the-art for eleven\\\\nNLP tasks. We also report extensive abla-\\\\ntions of BERT, demonstrating that the bidi-\\\\nrectional nature of our model is the single\\\\nmost important new contribution. The code\\\\nand pre-trained model will be available at\\\\ngoo.gl/language/bert.1\\\\n2\\\\nRelated Work\\\\nThere is a long history of pre-training general lan-\\\\nguage representations, and we brieﬂy review the\\\\nmost popular approaches in this section.\\\\n2.1\\\\nFeature-based Approaches\\\\nLearning widely applicable representations of\\\\nwords has been an active area of research for\\\\ndecades, including non-neural (Brown et al., 1992;\\\\n1Will be released before the end of October 2018.\\\\nAndo and Zhang, 2005; Blitzer et al., 2006) and\\\\nneural (Collobert and Weston, 2008; Mikolov\\\\net al., 2013; Pennington et al., 2014) methods. Pre-\\\\ntrained word embeddings are considered to be an\\\\nintegral part of modern NLP systems, offering sig-\\\\nniﬁcant improvements over embeddings learned\\\\nfrom scratch (Turian et al., 2010).\\\\nThese approaches have been generalized to\\\\ncoarser granularities, such as sentence embed-\\\\ndings (Kiros et al., 2015; Logeswaran and Lee,\\\\n2018) or paragraph embeddings (Le and Mikolov,\\\\n2014).\\\\nAs with traditional word embeddings,\\\\nthese learned representations are also typically\\\\nused as features in a downstream model.\\\\nELMo (Peters et al., 2017) generalizes tradi-\\\\ntional word embedding research along a differ-\\\\nent dimension. They propose to extract context-\\\\nsensitive features from a language model. When\\\\nintegrating contextual word embeddings with ex-\\\\nisting task-speciﬁc architectures, ELMo advances\\\\nthe state-of-the-art for several major NLP bench-\\\\nmarks (Peters et al., 2018) including question an-\\\\nswering (Rajpurkar et al., 2016) on SQuAD, sen-\\\\ntiment analysis (Socher et al., 2013), and named\\\\nentity recognition (Tjong Kim Sang and De Meul-\\\\nder, 2003).\\\\n2.2\\\\nFine-tuning Approaches\\\\nA recent trend in transfer learning from language\\\\nmodels (LMs) is to pre-train some model ar-\\\\nchitecture on a LM objective before ﬁne-tuning\\\\nthat same model for a supervised downstream\\\\ntask (Dai and Le, 2015; Howard and Ruder, 2018;\\\\nRadford et al., 2018). The advantage of these ap-\\\\nproaches is that few parameters need to be learned\\\\nfrom scratch. At least partly due this advantage,\\\\nOpenAI GPT (Radford et al., 2018) achieved pre-\\\\nviously state-of-the-art results on many sentence-\\\\nlevel tasks from the GLUE benchmark (Wang\\\\net al., 2018).\\\\n2.3\\\\nTransfer Learning from Supervised Data\\\\nWhile the advantage of unsupervised pre-training\\\\nis that there is a nearly unlimited amount of data\\\\navailable, there has also been work showing ef-\\\\nfective transfer from supervised tasks with large\\\\ndatasets, such as natural language inference (Con-\\\\nneau et al., 2017) and machine translation (Mc-\\\\nCann et al., 2017).\\\\nOutside of NLP, computer\\\\nvision research has also demonstrated the impor-\\\\ntance of transfer learning from large pre-trained\\\\nmodels, where an effective recipe is to ﬁne-tune\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 3 ===\\\\nBERT (Ours)\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\n...\\\\n...\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\nTrm\\\\n...\\\\n...\\\\nOpenAI GPT\\\\nLstm\\\\nELMo\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\nLstm\\\\n T1\\\\nT2\\\\n TN\\\\n...\\\\n...\\\\n...\\\\n...\\\\n...\\\\n E1\\\\nE2\\\\n EN\\\\n...\\\\n T1\\\\nT2\\\\nTN\\\\n...\\\\n E1\\\\nE2\\\\n EN\\\\n...\\\\n T1\\\\nT2\\\\n TN\\\\n...\\\\n E1\\\\nE2\\\\n EN\\\\n...\\\\nFigure 1: Differences in pre-training model architectures. (2017) as well as excellent guides such as\\\\n“The Annotated Transformer.”3\\\\nIn this work, we denote the number of layers\\\\n(i.e., Transformer blocks) as L, the hidden size as\\\\nH, and the number of self-attention heads as A.\\\\nIn all cases we set the feed-forward/ﬁlter size to\\\\nbe 4H, i.e., 3072 for the H = 768 and 4096 for\\\\nthe H = 1024. We primarily report results on two\\\\nmodel sizes:\\\\n• BERTBASE: L=12, H=768, A=12, Total Pa-\\\\nrameters=110M\\\\n2https://github.com/tensorﬂow/tensor2tensor\\\\n3http://nlp.seas.harvard.edu/2018/04/03/attention.html\\\\n• BERTLARGE: L=24, H=1024, A=16, Total\\\\nParameters=340M\\\\nBERTBASE was chosen to have an identical\\\\nmodel size as OpenAI GPT for comparison pur-\\\\nposes. Critically, however, the BERT Transformer\\\\nuses bidirectional self-attention, while the GPT\\\\nTransformer uses constrained self-attention where\\\\nevery token can only attend to context to its left.\\\\nWe note that in the literature the bidirectional\\\\nTransformer is often referred to as a “Transformer\\\\nencoder” while the left-context-only version is re-\\\\nferred to as a “Transformer decoder” since it can\\\\nbe used for text generation. The comparisons be-\\\\ntween BERT, OpenAI GPT and ELMo are shown\\\\nvisually in Figure 1.\\\\n3.2\\\\nInput Representation\\\\nOur input representation is able to unambiguously\\\\nrepresent both a single text sentence or a pair of\\\\ntext sentences (e.g., [Question, Answer]) in one\\\\ntoken sequence.4 For a given token, its input rep-\\\\nresentation is constructed by summing the cor-\\\\nresponding token, segment and position embed-\\\\ndings. A visual representation of our input rep-\\\\nresentation is given in Figure 2.\\\\nThe speciﬁcs are:\\\\n• We use WordPiece embeddings (Wu et al.,\\\\n2016) with a 30,000 token vocabulary. We\\\\ndenote split word pieces with ##.\\\\n• We use learned positional embeddings with\\\\nsupported sequence lengths up to 512 tokens.\\\\n4Throughout this work, a “sentence” can be an arbitrary\\\\nspan of contiguous text, rather than an actual linguistic sen-\\\\ntence. A “sequence” refers to the input token sequence to\\\\nBERT, which may be a single sentence or two sentences\\\\npacked together.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 4 ===\\\\n[CLS]\\\\nhe\\\\nlikes\\\\nplay\\\\n##ing\\\\n[SEP]\\\\nmy\\\\ndog\\\\nis\\\\ncute\\\\n[SEP]\\\\nInput\\\\nE[CLS]\\\\nEhe\\\\nElikes\\\\nEplay\\\\nE##ing\\\\nE[SEP]\\\\nEmy\\\\nEdog\\\\nEis\\\\nEcute\\\\nE[SEP]\\\\nToken\\\\nEmbeddings\\\\nEA\\\\nEB\\\\nEB\\\\nEB\\\\nEB\\\\nEB\\\\nEA\\\\nEA\\\\nEA\\\\nEA\\\\nEA\\\\nSegment\\\\nEmbeddings\\\\nE0\\\\nE6\\\\nE7\\\\nE8\\\\nE9\\\\nE10\\\\nE1\\\\nE2\\\\nE3\\\\nE4\\\\nE5\\\\nPosition\\\\nEmbeddings\\\\nFigure 2: BERT input representation. The input embeddings is the sum of the token embeddings, the segmentation\\\\nembeddings and the position embeddings.\\\\n• The ﬁrst token of every sequence is al-\\\\nways the special classiﬁcation embedding\\\\n([CLS]). The ﬁnal hidden state (i.e., out-\\\\nput of Transformer) corresponding to this to-\\\\nken is used as the aggregate sequence rep-\\\\nresentation for classiﬁcation tasks. For non-\\\\nclassiﬁcation tasks, this vector is ignored.\\\\n• Sentence pairs are packed together into a sin-\\\\ngle sequence. We differentiate the sentences\\\\nin two ways. First, we separate them with\\\\na special token ([SEP]). Second, we add a\\\\nlearned sentence A embedding to every token\\\\nof the ﬁrst sentence and a sentence B embed-\\\\nding to every token of the second sentence.\\\\n• For single-sentence inputs we only use the\\\\nsentence A embeddings.\\\\n3.3\\\\nPre-training Tasks\\\\nUnlike Peters et al. (2018) and Radford et al.\\\\n(2018), we do not use traditional left-to-right or\\\\nright-to-left language models to pre-train BERT.\\\\nInstead, we pre-train BERT using two novel unsu-\\\\npervised prediction tasks, described in this section.\\\\n3.3.1\\\\nTask #1: Masked LM\\\\nIntuitively, it is reasonable to believe that a\\\\ndeep bidirectional model is strictly more power-\\\\nful than either a left-to-right model or the shal-\\\\nlow concatenation of a left-to-right and right-to-\\\\nleft model.\\\\nUnfortunately, standard conditional\\\\nlanguage models can only be trained left-to-right\\\\nor right-to-left, since bidirectional conditioning\\\\nwould allow each word to indirectly “see itself”\\\\nin a multi-layered context.\\\\nIn order to train a deep bidirectional representa-\\\\ntion, we take a straightforward approach of mask-\\\\ning some percentage of the input tokens at random,\\\\nand then predicting only those masked tokens. We\\\\nrefer to this procedure as a “masked LM” (MLM),\\\\nalthough it is often referred to as a Cloze task in\\\\nthe literature (Taylor, 1953). In this case, the ﬁ-\\\\nnal hidden vectors corresponding to the mask to-\\\\nkens are fed into an output softmax over the vo-\\\\ncabulary, as in a standard LM. In all of our exper-\\\\niments, we mask 15% of all WordPiece tokens in\\\\neach sequence at random. In contrast to denoising\\\\nauto-encoders (Vincent et al., 2008), we only pre-\\\\ndict the masked words rather than reconstructing\\\\nthe entire input.\\\\nAlthough this does allow us to obtain a bidirec-\\\\ntional pre-trained model, there are two downsides\\\\nto such an approach. The ﬁrst is that we are cre-\\\\nating a mismatch between pre-training and ﬁne-\\\\ntuning, since the [MASK] token is never seen dur-\\\\ning ﬁne-tuning. To mitigate this, we do not always\\\\nreplace “masked” words with the actual [MASK]\\\\ntoken. Instead, the training data generator chooses\\\\n15% of tokens at random, e.g., in the sentence my\\\\ndog is hairy it chooses hairy. It then performs\\\\nthe following procedure:\\\\n• Rather than always replacing the chosen\\\\nwords with [MASK], the data generator will\\\\ndo the following:\\\\n• 80% of the time: Replace the word with the\\\\n[MASK] token, e.g., my dog is hairy →\\\\nmy dog is [MASK]\\\\n• 10% of the time: Replace the word with a\\\\nrandom word, e.g., my dog is hairy →my\\\\ndog is apple\\\\n• 10% of the time:\\\\nKeep the word un-\\\\nchanged, e.g., my dog is hairy →my dog\\\\nis hairy. The purpose of this is to bias the\\\\nrepresentation towards the actual observed\\\\nword.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 5 ===\\\\nThe Transformer encoder does not know which\\\\nwords it will be asked to predict or which have\\\\nbeen replaced by random words, so it is forced to\\\\nkeep a distributional contextual representation of\\\\nevery input token. Additionally, because random\\\\nreplacement only occurs for 1.5% of all tokens\\\\n(i.e., 10% of 15%), this does not seem to harm the\\\\nmodel’s language understanding capability.\\\\nThe second downside of using an MLM is that\\\\nonly 15% of tokens are predicted in each batch,\\\\nwhich suggests that more pre-training steps may\\\\nbe required for the model to converge. In Sec-\\\\ntion 5.3 we demonstrate that MLM does con-\\\\nverge marginally slower than a left-to-right model\\\\n(which predicts every token), but the empirical im-\\\\nprovements of the MLM model far outweigh the\\\\nincreased training cost.\\\\n3.3.2\\\\nTask #2: Next Sentence Prediction\\\\nMany important downstream tasks such as Ques-\\\\ntion Answering (QA) and Natural Language In-\\\\nference (NLI) are based on understanding the re-\\\\nlationship between two text sentences, which is\\\\nnot directly captured by language modeling. In\\\\norder to train a model that understands sentence\\\\nrelationships, we pre-train a binarized next sen-\\\\ntence prediction task that can be trivially gener-\\\\nated from any monolingual corpus. Speciﬁcally,\\\\nwhen choosing the sentences A and B for each pre-\\\\ntraining example, 50% of the time B is the actual\\\\nnext sentence that follows A, and 50% of the time\\\\nit is a random sentence from the corpus. For ex-\\\\nample:\\\\nInput = [CLS] the man went to [MASK] store [SEP]\\\\nhe bought a gallon [MASK] milk [SEP]\\\\nLabel = IsNext\\\\nInput = [CLS] the man [MASK] to the store [SEP]\\\\npenguin [MASK] are flight ##less birds [SEP]\\\\nLabel = NotNext\\\\nWe choose the NotNext sentences completely at\\\\nrandom, and the ﬁnal pre-trained model achieves\\\\n97%-98% accuracy at this task. Despite its sim-\\\\nplicity, we demonstrate in Section 5.1 that pre-\\\\ntraining towards this task is very beneﬁcial to both\\\\nQA and NLI.\\\\n3.4\\\\nPre-training Procedure\\\\nThe pre-training procedure largely follows the ex-\\\\nisting literature on language model pre-training.\\\\nFor the pre-training corpus we use the concatena-\\\\ntion of BooksCorpus (800M words) (Zhu et al.,\\\\n2015) and English Wikipedia (2,500M words).\\\\nFor Wikipedia we extract only the text passages\\\\nand ignore lists, tables, and headers. It is criti-\\\\ncal to use a document-level corpus rather than a\\\\nshufﬂed sentence-level corpus such as the Billion\\\\nWord Benchmark (Chelba et al., 2013) in order to\\\\nextract long contiguous sequences.\\\\nTo generate each training input sequence, we\\\\nsample two spans of text from the corpus, which\\\\nwe refer to as “sentences” even though they are\\\\ntypically much longer than single sentences (but\\\\ncan be shorter also). The ﬁrst sentence receives\\\\nthe A embedding and the second receives the B\\\\nembedding. 50% of the time B is the actual next\\\\nsentence that follows A and 50% of the time it is\\\\na random sentence, which is done for the “next\\\\nsentence prediction” task. They are sampled such\\\\nthat the combined length is ≤512 tokens. The\\\\nLM masking is applied after WordPiece tokeniza-\\\\ntion with a uniform masking rate of 15%, and no\\\\nspecial consideration given to partial word pieces.\\\\nWe train with batch size of 256 sequences (256\\\\nsequences * 512 tokens = 128,000 tokens/batch)\\\\nfor 1,000,000 steps, which is approximately 40\\\\nepochs over the 3.3 billion word corpus.\\\\nWe\\\\nuse Adam with learning rate of 1e-4, β1 = 0.9,\\\\nβ2 = 0.999, L2 weight decay of 0.01, learning\\\\nrate warmup over the ﬁrst 10,000 steps, and linear\\\\ndecay of the learning rate. We use a dropout prob-\\\\nability of 0.1 on all layers. We use a gelu acti-\\\\nvation (Hendrycks and Gimpel, 2016) rather than\\\\nthe standard relu, following OpenAI GPT. The\\\\ntraining loss is the sum of the mean masked LM\\\\nlikelihood and mean next sentence prediction like-\\\\nlihood.\\\\nTraining of BERTBASE was performed on 4\\\\nCloud TPUs in Pod conﬁguration (16 TPU chips\\\\ntotal).5 Training of BERTLARGE was performed\\\\non 16 Cloud TPUs (64 TPU chips total). Each pre-\\\\ntraining took 4 days to complete.\\\\n3.5\\\\nFine-tuning Procedure\\\\nFor sequence-level classiﬁcation tasks, BERT\\\\nﬁne-tuning is straightforward. In order to obtain\\\\na ﬁxed-dimensional pooled representation of the\\\\ninput sequence, we take the ﬁnal hidden state (i.e.,\\\\nthe output of the Transformer) for the ﬁrst token\\\\n5https://cloudplatform.googleblog.com/2018/06/Cloud-\\\\nTPU-now-offers-preemptible-pricing-and-global-\\\\navailability.html\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 6 ===\\\\nin the input, which by construction corresponds to\\\\nthe the special [CLS] word embedding. We de-\\\\nnote this vector as C ∈RH. The only new pa-\\\\nrameters added during ﬁne-tuning are for a classi-\\\\nﬁcation layer W ∈RK×H, where K is the num-\\\\nber of classiﬁer labels.\\\\nThe label probabilities\\\\nP ∈RK are computed with a standard softmax,\\\\nP = softmax(CW T ). All of the parameters of\\\\nBERT and W are ﬁne-tuned jointly to maximize\\\\nthe log-probability of the correct label. For span-\\\\nlevel and token-level prediction tasks, the above\\\\nprocedure must be modiﬁed slightly in a task-\\\\nspeciﬁc manner. Details are given in the corre-\\\\nsponding subsection of Section 4.\\\\nFor ﬁne-tuning, most model hyperparameters\\\\nare the same as in pre-training, with the excep-\\\\ntion of the batch size, learning rate, and number\\\\nof training epochs. The dropout probability was\\\\nalways kept at 0.1. The optimal hyperparameter\\\\nvalues are task-speciﬁc, but we found the follow-\\\\ning range of possible values to work well across\\\\nall tasks:\\\\n• Batch size: 16, 32\\\\n• Learning rate (Adam): 5e-5, 3e-5, 2e-5\\\\n• Number of epochs: 3, 4\\\\nWe also observed that large data sets (e.g.,\\\\n100k+ labeled training examples) were far less\\\\nsensitive to hyperparameter choice than small data\\\\nsets. Fine-tuning is typically very fast, so it is rea-\\\\nsonable to simply run an exhaustive search over\\\\nthe above parameters and choose the model that\\\\nperforms best on the development set.\\\\n3.6\\\\nComparison of BERT and OpenAI GPT\\\\nThe most comparable existing pre-training method\\\\nto BERT is OpenAI GPT, which trains a left-to-\\\\nright Transformer LM on a large text corpus. In\\\\nfact, many of the design decisions in BERT were\\\\nintentionally chosen to be as close to GPT as pos-\\\\nsible so that the two methods could be minimally\\\\ncompared. The core argument of this work is that\\\\nthe two novel pre-training tasks presented in Sec-\\\\ntion 3.3 account for the majority of the empiri-\\\\ncal improvements, but we do note that there are\\\\nseveral other differences between how BERT and\\\\nGPT were trained:\\\\n• GPT is trained on the BooksCorpus (800M\\\\nwords); BERT is trained on the BooksCor-\\\\npus (800M words) and Wikipedia (2,500M\\\\nwords).\\\\n• GPT uses a sentence separator ([SEP]) and\\\\nclassiﬁer token ([CLS]) which are only in-\\\\ntroduced at ﬁne-tuning time; BERT learns\\\\n[SEP], [CLS] and sentence A/B embed-\\\\ndings during pre-training.\\\\n• GPT was trained for 1M steps with a batch\\\\nsize of 32,000 words; BERT was trained for\\\\n1M steps with a batch size of 128,000 words.\\\\n• GPT used the same learning rate of 5e-5 for\\\\nall ﬁne-tuning experiments; BERT chooses a\\\\ntask-speciﬁc ﬁne-tuning learning rate which\\\\nperforms the best on the development set.\\\\nTo isolate the effect of these differences, we per-\\\\nform ablation experiments in Section 5.1 which\\\\ndemonstrate that the majority of the improvements\\\\nare in fact coming from the new pre-training tasks.\\\\n4\\\\nExperiments\\\\nIn this section, we present BERT ﬁne-tuning re-\\\\nsults on 11 NLP tasks.\\\\n4.1\\\\nGLUE Datasets\\\\nThe General Language Understanding Evaluation\\\\n(GLUE) benchmark (Wang et al., 2018) is a col-\\\\nlection of diverse natural language understand-\\\\ning tasks. As AI applications are growing rapidly,\\\\nso are the number of embeddings that need to be\\\\nstored and indexed. The Faiss library is dedicated to\\\\nvector similarity search, a core functionality of vector\\\\ndatabases. Faiss is a toolkit of indexing methods and\\\\nrelated primitives used to search, cluster, compress\\\\nand transform vectors. This paper first describes the\\\\ntradeoff space of vector search, then the design prin-\\\\nciples of Faiss in terms of structure, approach to opti-\\\\nmization and interfacing. We benchmark key features\\\\nof the library and discuss a few selected applications\\\\nto highlight its broad applicability.\\\\n1\\\\nIntroduction\\\\nThe emergence of deep learning has induced a shift in\\\\nhow complex data is stored and searched, noticeably\\\\nby the development of embeddings. Embeddings are\\\\nvector representations, typically produced by a neural\\\\nnetwork, whose main objective is to map (embed)\\\\nthe input media item into a vector space, where the\\\\nlocality encodes the semantics of the input. Embed-\\\\ndings are extracted from various forms of media:\\\\nwords [Mikolov et al., 2013, Bojanowski et al., 2017],\\\\ntext\\\\n[Devlin et al., 2018,\\\\nIzacard et al., 2021],\\\\nim-\\\\nages\\\\n[Caron et al., 2021,\\\\nPizzi et al., 2022],\\\\nusers\\\\nand\\\\nitems\\\\nfor\\\\nrecommendation\\\\n[Paterek, 2007].\\\\nThey can even encode object relations,\\\\nfor in-\\\\nstance multi-modal text-image or text-audio rela-\\\\ntions [Duquenne et al., 2023, Radford et al., 2021].\\\\nEmbeddings are employed as an intermediate\\\\nrepresentation\\\\nfor\\\\nfurther\\\\nprocessing,\\\\ne.g.\\\\nself-\\\\nsupervised image embeddings can input to shal-\\\\nlow supervised image classifiers [Caron et al., 2018,\\\\nCaron et al., 2021].\\\\nThey are also leveraged as\\\\na pretext task for self-supervision,\\\\ne.g. in Sim-\\\\nCLR [Chen et al., 2020]. The purpose that we consider\\\\nin this paper is when embeddings are used directly\\\\nto compare media items.\\\\nThe embedding extractor\\\\nis designed such that the distance between embed-\\\\ndings reflects the similarity between their correspond-\\\\ning media. As a result, neighborhood search in this\\\\nvector space offers a direct implementation of similar-\\\\nity search between media items.\\\\nEmbeddings are popular in industrial setting for\\\\ntasks where end-to-end learning would not be cost-\\\\nefficient.\\\\nFor example, a k nearest-neighbor classi-\\\\nfier is more efficient to upgrade than a classification\\\\ndeep neural net. In that case, embeddings are par-\\\\nticularly useful as a compact intermediate representa-\\\\ntion that can be re-used for several purposes. This ex-\\\\nplains why industrial database management systems\\\\n(DBMS) that offer a vector storage and search func-\\\\ntionality have gained adoption in the last years. These\\\\nDBMS are at the junction of traditional databases and\\\\nApproximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) algo-\\\\nrithms. Until recently, the latter were mostly consid-\\\\nered for specific use-cases or in research.\\\\nFrom a practical point of view, there are multiple\\\\nadvantages to maintain a clear separation of roles be-\\\\ntween the embedding extraction and the vector search\\\\nalgorithm. Both are bound by an “embedding con-\\\\ntract” on the embedding distance:\\\\n• The embedding extractor, which is typically a\\\\nneural network in modern systems, is trained so\\\\nthat distances between embeddings are aligned\\\\nwith the task to perform.\\\\n• The vector index aims at performing neighbor\\\\nsearch among the embedding vectors as accu-\\\\nrately as possible w.r.t. exact search results given\\\\nthe agreed distance metric.\\\\nFaiss is an industrial-grade library for ANNS. It is\\\\ndesigned to be used both from simple scripts and as\\\\na building block of a DBMS. In contrast with other li-\\\\nbraries that focus on a single indexing method, Faiss\\\\nis a toolbox that contains indexing methods that com-\\\\nmonly involve a chain of components (preprocessing,\\\\ncompression, non-exhaustive search, etc.). This is nec-\\\\nessary: depending on the usage constraints, the most\\\\nefficient indexing methods are different.\\\\nLet us also summarize what Faiss is not: Faiss does\\\\nnot extract features – it only indexes embeddings that\\\\nhave been extracted by a different mechanism; Faiss\\\\nis not a service – it only provides functions that are\\\\n1\\\\narXiv:2401.08281v1  [cs.LG]  16 Jan 2024\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 2 ===\\\\nrun as part of the calling process on the local machine;\\\\nFaiss is not a database – it does not provide concur-\\\\nrent write access, load balancing, sharding, consis-\\\\ntency. The scope of the library is intentionally limited\\\\nto focus on carefully implemented algorithms.\\\\nThe basic structure of Faiss is the index. An index\\\\ncan store a number of database vectors that are progres-\\\\nsively added to it. At search time, a query vector is sub-\\\\nmitted to the index. The index returns the database\\\\nvector that is closest to the query vector in terms of\\\\nEuclidean distance. There are many variants of this\\\\nbasic functionality: instead of just the nearest neigh-\\\\nbor, k nearest neighbors can be returned; instead of a\\\\nfixed number of neighbors, only the vectors within a\\\\ncertain range can be returned; several vectors can be\\\\nsearched in parallel, in a batch mode; metrics other\\\\nthan the Euclidean distance are supported; the accu-\\\\nracy of search can be traded for speed or memory. The\\\\nsearch can use either CPUs or GPUs.\\\\nThe objective of this paper is to expose the de-\\\\nsign principles of Faiss.\\\\nA similarity search library\\\\nhas to strike a tradeoff between different constraints\\\\n(Section 3), which is addressed in Faiss with two\\\\nmain tools: vector compression (Section 4) and non-\\\\nexhaustive search (Section 5). Faiss is engineered to\\\\nbe flexible and usable from other tools (Section 7). We\\\\nalso review a few applications of Faiss for trillion-\\\\nscale indexing, text retrieval, data mining, and con-\\\\ntent moderation (Section 8). Throughout, we will re-\\\\nfer with a specific style to functions or classes in the\\\\nFaiss codebase1 and documentation2.\\\\n2\\\\nRelated work\\\\nIndexing methods.\\\\nIn the last decade, there has\\\\nbeen a steady stream of papers about indexing meth-\\\\nods that were published together with their reference\\\\nimplementations. In Faiss, we consider in particular\\\\nalgorithms that cover a wide spectrum of use-cases.\\\\nOne of the most popular approach in industry is to\\\\nemploy Locality Sensitive Hashing as a way to com-\\\\npress embeddings into compact codes.\\\\nIn particu-\\\\nlar, the Cosine sketch [Charikar, 2002] produces bi-\\\\nnary vectors such that, in the corresponding Ham-\\\\nming space, the Hamming distance is an estimator\\\\nof the cosine similarity between the original embed-\\\\ndings. The compactness of these sketches enables stor-\\\\ning and therefore searching very large databases of\\\\nmedia content [Lv et al., 2004], without the require-\\\\nment to store the original embeddings. We refer the\\\\nreader the early survey by [Wang et al., 2015] for re-\\\\nsearch on binary codes.\\\\nSince the work by [J´egou et al., 2010], ANN based\\\\non quantization has emerged as a powerful alter-\\\\nnative to binary codes [Wang et al., 2017].\\\\nWe re-\\\\nfer the reader to the survey by [Matsui et al., 2018]\\\\nthat discusses numerous research works related to\\\\nquantization-based compact codes.\\\\n1https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss\\\\n2https://faiss.ai/\\\\nLSH is also often referring to indexing with mul-\\\\ntiple partitions, such as E2LSH [Datar et al., 2004].\\\\nWe do no consider them because they are not\\\\nperforming as well as learned partitions on real\\\\ndata [Paulev´e et al., 2010].\\\\nEarly data-aware meth-\\\\nods that proved successful on large datasets include\\\\nmultiple partitions based on kd-tree or hierarchical k-\\\\nmeans in [Muja and Lowe, 2014]. They are often com-\\\\nbined with compressed-domain representation and\\\\nare especially appropriate for very large-scale set-\\\\ntings [Jegou et al., 2008, J´egou et al., 2010].\\\\nAfter the introduction of the NN-descent algo-\\\\nrithm [Dong et al., 2011], ANN algorithms based on\\\\ngraphs have emerged as a viable alternative to meth-\\\\nods based on space partitioning.\\\\nIn particular\\\\nHNSW, which is the most popular current indexing\\\\nmethod [Malkov and Yashunin, 2018] for medium-\\\\nsized dataset is implemented in HNSWlib.\\\\nSoftware packages.\\\\nMost of the research works on\\\\nvector search were open-sourced, and some of these\\\\nevolved in relatively comprehensive software pack-\\\\nages for vector search. FLANN includes several in-\\\\ndex types and a distributed implementation described\\\\nextensively in the paper [Muja and Lowe, 2014]. The\\\\nfirst implementation of product quantization relied\\\\non the Yael library [Douze and J´egou, 2014], that al-\\\\nready had a few of the Faiss principles:\\\\nopti-\\\\nmized primitives for clustering methods (GMM and\\\\nk-means), scripting language interface (Matlab and\\\\nPython) and benchmarking operators.\\\\nThe NM-\\\\nSlib package, intended for text retrieval was the\\\\nfirst package to include HNSW [Boytsov et al., 2016]\\\\nand also offers several index types.\\\\nThe HNSWlib\\\\nlibrary later became the reference implementation\\\\nof HNSW [Malkov and Yashunin, 2018].\\\\nGoogle’s\\\\nSCANN library is mainly a thoroughly optimized im-\\\\nplementation of IVFPQ [J´egou et al., 2010] on SIMD\\\\nand includes several index variants for various\\\\ndatabase scales. SCANN was open-sourced together\\\\nwith the paper [Guo et al., 2020], which does not de-\\\\nscribe what makes the library so fast: its engineer-\\\\ning optimization. Diskann [Subramanya et al., 2019]\\\\nis Microsoft’s foundational graph-based vector search\\\\nlibrary, initially built to exploit hybrid RAM/flash\\\\nmemory,\\\\nbut that also offers a RAM-only ver-\\\\nsion called Vamana.\\\\nIt was later extended to\\\\nperform efficient updates [Singh et al., 2021], out-of-\\\\ndistribution searches [Jaiswal et al., 2022] and filtered\\\\nsearches [Gollapudi et al., 2023].\\\\nFaiss was open-sourced simultaneously with the re-\\\\nlease of the paper [Johnson et al., 2019] that describes\\\\nthe GPU implementation of several index types. The\\\\npresent paper complements this previous work by de-\\\\nscribing the library as a whole.\\\\nIn parallel, numerous software libraries from the\\\\ndatabase world were extended or developed to do\\\\nvector search.\\\\nMilvus [Wang et al., 2021] uses its\\\\nKnowhere library, which relies on Faiss as one of its\\\\ncore engines. Pinecone [Bruch et al., 2023] initially re-\\\\n2\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 3 ===\\\\nlied on Faiss. The engine has since been rewritten.\\\\nWeaviate [van Luijt and Verhagen, 2020] is a compos-\\\\nite retrieval engine that includes vector search.\\\\nBenchmarks\\\\nand\\\\ncompetitions.\\\\nThe\\\\nleading\\\\nbenchmark\\\\nfor\\\\nmillion-scale\\\\ndatasets\\\\nis\\\\nANN-\\\\nbenchmarks\\\\n[Aum¨uller et al., 2020]\\\\nthat\\\\nnow\\\\ncompares\\\\nabout\\\\n50\\\\nimplementations\\\\nof\\\\nANNS.\\\\nThis\\\\nbenchmark\\\\nwas\\\\nupgraded\\\\nwith\\\\nthe\\\\nbig-\\\\nANN [Simhadri et al., 2022a] challenge, that includes\\\\n6 datasets with 1 billion vectors each.\\\\nFaiss was\\\\nused as a baseline for the challenge and multiple\\\\nsubmissions derived from Faiss. The 2023’s edition of\\\\nthe challenge is at a more modest scale (10M vectors)\\\\nbut the tasks are more elaborate. For instance there is\\\\na filtered track for which Faiss was a baseline method.\\\\nDatasets\\\\nThe datasets used to evaluate vector search\\\\nare typical for the tasks that vector search per-\\\\nforms.\\\\nEarly datasets are based on keypoint fea-\\\\ntures like SIFT [Lowe, 2004] used in image match-\\\\ning.\\\\nWe\\\\nuse\\\\nBIGANN\\\\n[J´egou et al., 2011b],\\\\na\\\\ndataset of 128-dimensional SIFT features.\\\\nLater,\\\\nwhen global image descriptors produced by neu-\\\\nral nets became popular, the Deep1B dataset was\\\\nreleased\\\\n[Babenko and Lempitsky, 2016],\\\\nwith\\\\n96-\\\\ndimensional image features extracted with Google\\\\nLeNet [Szegedy et al., 2015]. For this paper we intro-\\\\nduce a dataset of 768-dimensional Contriever text em-\\\\nbeddings [Izacard et al., 2021] that are compared with\\\\ninner product similarity. The embeddings are com-\\\\nputed on English Wikipedia passages. The higher di-\\\\nmension of these embeddings is typical for contempo-\\\\nrary applications.\\\\nEach dataset has 10k query vectors, 20M to 350M\\\\ntraining vectors. We indicate the size of the database\\\\nexplicitly, for example “Deep1M” means the database\\\\ncontains the 1M first vectors of deep1B. The training,\\\\ndatabase and query vectors are sampled randomly\\\\nfrom the same distribution, we don’t address out-\\\\nof-distribution data in this paper [Jaiswal et al., 2022,\\\\nBaranchuk et al., 2023].\\\\n3\\\\nPerformance axes of a vector\\\\nsearch library\\\\nVector search is a well-defined, unambiguous oper-\\\\nation.\\\\nIn its simplest formulation, given a set of\\\\ndatabase vectors {xi, i = 1..N} ⊂Rd and a query vec-\\\\ntor q ∈Rd, it computes\\\\nn = argmin\\\\nn=1..N\\\\n∥q −xn∥\\\\n(1)\\\\nThis can be computed with a direct algorithm by iter-\\\\nating over all database vectors: this is brute force search.\\\\nA slightly more general and complex operation is to\\\\ncompute the k nearest neighbors of q:\\\\n(n1, ..., nk) = k −argmin\\\\nn=1..N\\\\n∥q −xn∥\\\\n(2)\\\\nThis is what the search method of a Faiss index re-\\\\nturns. A related operation is to find all the elements\\\\nthat are within some distance ε to the query:\\\\nR = {n = 1..N s.t. ∥q −xn∥≤ε},\\\\n(3)\\\\nwhich is computed with the range search method.\\\\nDistance measures.\\\\nIn the equations above, we\\\\nleave the definition of the distance undefined. The\\\\nmost commonly used distances in Faiss are the L2 dis-\\\\ntance, the cosine similarity and the inner product simi-\\\\nlarity (for the latter two the argmin should be replaced\\\\nwith an argmax). These simple measures have useful\\\\nanalytical properties: for example, they are invariant\\\\nunder d-dimensional rotations.\\\\nThere are many relationships between the mea-\\\\nsures. They can be made equivalent by preprocess-\\\\ning transformations on the query and/or the database\\\\nvectors. Table 1 summarizes the preprocessing trans-\\\\nformations that are applicable for various bridges.\\\\nSome were already identified [Bachrach et al., 2014,\\\\nHong et al., 2019], others are new.\\\\nNote\\\\nthat\\\\nvectors\\\\ntransformed\\\\nin\\\\nthis\\\\nway\\\\nhave\\\\na\\\\nvery\\\\nanisotropic\\\\ndistribu-\\\\ntion\\\\n[Morozov and Babenko, 2018]\\\\nand\\\\ncan\\\\nbe\\\\n“harder” to index. In particular, for product or scalar\\\\nquantization, the additional dimension incurred for\\\\nmany transformations is not homogeneous with other\\\\ndimensions. See Section 4.2 for mitigations.\\\\n3.1\\\\nBrute force search\\\\nImplementing brute force search efficiently is not triv-\\\\nial [Chern et al., 2022, Johnson et al., 2019]. It requires\\\\n(1) an efficient way of computing the distances and\\\\n(2) for k-nearest neighbor search, an efficient way of\\\\nkeeping track of the k smallest distances.\\\\nComputing distances in Faiss is performed either by\\\\ndirect distances computations, or, when query vectors\\\\nare provided in large enough batches, using a matrix\\\\nmultiplication\\\\ndecomposition\\\\n[Johnson et al., 2019,\\\\nequation 2]. The Faiss functions are exposed in knn\\\\nand knn gpu for CPU and GPU respectively.\\\\nCollecting\\\\nthe\\\\ntop-k\\\\nsmallest\\\\ndistances\\\\nis\\\\nusually\\\\ndone\\\\nvia\\\\na\\\\nbinary\\\\nheap\\\\non\\\\nCPU\\\\n[Douze and J´egou, 2014,\\\\nsection\\\\n2.1]\\\\nor\\\\na\\\\nsorting\\\\nnetwork\\\\non\\\\nGPU\\\\n[Johnson et al., 2019,\\\\nOotomo et al., 2023]. For larger values of k, it is more\\\\nefficient to use a reservoir: an unordered result buffer\\\\nof size k′ > k that is resized to k when it overflows.\\\\nBrute-force search gives accurate results. However,\\\\nfor large, high-dimensional datasets this approach be-\\\\ncomes slow. In low dimensions, there are branch-and-\\\\nbound methods that yield exact search results. How-\\\\never, in large dimensions they provide no speedup\\\\nover brute force search [Weber et al., 1998].\\\\nIn these cases, we have to resort to approximate\\\\nnearest neighbor search (ANNS).\\\\n3\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 4 ===\\\\nindex metric →\\\\nL2\\\\nIP\\\\ncos\\\\nwanted metric ↓\\\\nL2\\\\nidentity\\\\nx′ = [x; −α/2]\\\\ny′ = [y; ∥y∥2/α]\\\\nx′ = [x; −α/2; 0]\\\\ny′ = [βy; β∥y∥2/α;\\\\np\\\\n1 −β2∥y∥2 −β2∥y∥4/α2]\\\\nIP\\\\nx′ = [x; 0]\\\\ny′ = [y;\\\\np\\\\nα2 −∥y∥2]\\\\nidentity\\\\nx′ = [x; 0]\\\\ny′ = [αy;\\\\np\\\\n1 −∥αy∥2]\\\\ncos\\\\nx′ = x/∥x∥\\\\ny′ = y/∥y∥\\\\nx′ = x/∥x∥\\\\ny′ = y/∥y∥\\\\nidentity\\\\nTable 1: One wants to search for a query vector x among database vector y given a particular metric (rows). The\\\\ndatabase may be preprocessed into an indexing struc-\\\\nture, rather than just being stored as a plain matrix.\\\\nAccuracy metrics.\\\\nIn ANNS the accuracy is mea-\\\\nsured as a difference with the exact search results.\\\\nNote that this is an intermediate goal: the end-to-end\\\\naccuracy depends on (1) how well the distance metric\\\\ncorrelates with the item matching objective and (2) the\\\\nquality of ANNS, which is what we measure here.\\\\nThis accuracy metric is compared to the ground-\\\\ntruth results from Equation (1).\\\\nThe accuracy for k-nearest neighbor search is gen-\\\\nerally evaluated as the “n-recall@m”, which is the\\\\nfraction of the n ground-truth nearest neighbors that\\\\nare in the m first search results.\\\\nMost often n = 1\\\\nor n = m (in which case the measure is a.k.a. “in-\\\\ntersection measure”).\\\\nWhen n = m = 1, the recall\\\\nmeasure and intersection are the same, and the re-\\\\ncall is called “accuracy”.\\\\nNote, in some publica-\\\\ntions [J´egou et al., 2010], recall@n means 1-recall@n,\\\\nwhile in others [Simhadri et al., 2022b] it corresponds\\\\nto n-recall@n.\\\\nFor range search, there are two thresholds:\\\\nthe\\\\nground-truth threshold ε of Equation 3 and a sec-\\\\nond threshold ε′ applied at search time. By sweep-\\\\ning ε′ from small to large, the result list bR increases.\\\\nComparing the search-time bR with the ground-truth\\\\nR yield a precision and recall, so the sweep produces\\\\na precision-recall curve. The area under the PR-curve\\\\nis the mean average precision score of range search.\\\\nFor vector codecs, the metric of choice is the mean\\\\nsquared error (MSE) between the original vector and\\\\nthe reconstructed vector. For an encoder C and a de-\\\\ncoder D, the MSE is:\\\\nMSE = Ex\\\\n\\\\u0002\\\\n∥D(C(x)) −x∥2\\\\n2\\\\n\\\\u0003\\\\n(4)\\\\nResource metrics.\\\\nThe other axes of the tradeoff are\\\\nrelated to computing resources. During search, the\\\\nsearch time and memory usage are the main con-\\\\nstraints, the experiments in this paper operate mainly\\\\nwith these. The memory usage can be smaller than\\\\nthat of the original vectors, if compression is used.\\\\nThe index may need to store training data, which\\\\nincurs a constant memory overhead before any vector\\\\nis added to the index. The index can also add per-\\\\nvector memory overhead to the memory used to store\\\\neach vector. This is the case for graph indexes, that\\\\nneed to store a graph for each node.\\\\nThe index building time is also a resource con-\\\\nstraint. It may be decomposed into a training time,\\\\na fixed cost that needs to be paid regardless of the\\\\nnumber of vectors added to the index and the addi-\\\\ntion time per vector.\\\\nThe memory usage is more complex to grasp for set-\\\\ntings with hybrid storage, for example RAM + flash +\\\\ndisk or GPU memory + RAM. In that case, there is\\\\nusually a small amount of fast memory and a larger\\\\namount of slower memory, so several access speeds\\\\nneed to be taken into account.\\\\nIn distributed settings or flash-backed storage,\\\\nthe relevant metric is the number of I/O opera-\\\\ntions (IOPS). Every read operation fetches a whole\\\\npage (of e.g. 4 kiB). Therefore, random accesses to\\\\nscalar elements are particularly inefficient.\\\\nIt is\\\\nbetter to organize the data layout to minimize the\\\\nIOPs [Subramanya et al., 2019].\\\\nAnother low-level\\\\nmetric is the amount of extra memory needed to\\\\npre-compute lookup tables used to speed up search,\\\\nwhich can be a limiting factor.\\\\n3.3\\\\nTradeoffs\\\\nMost often only a subset of metrics matter. For ex-\\\\nample, when a very large number of searches are per-\\\\nformed on a fixed index, index building time does\\\\nnot matter. Or when the number of vectors is so small\\\\nthat the raw database fits in RAM multiple times, then\\\\nmemory usage does not matter. We call the metrics\\\\nthat we care about the active constraints. Note that ac-\\\\ncuracy is always an active constraint because it can be\\\\ntraded off against every single other constraint. In ex-\\\\ntreme cases where accuracy does not matter, an index\\\\nthat returns random results would be sufficient (and\\\\nFaiss does actually provide an IndexRandom used in\\\\nsome benchmarking tasks).\\\\n4\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 5 ===\\\\n0.15\\\\n0.20\\\\n0.25\\\\n0.30\\\\n0.35\\\\n0.40\\\\nAccuracy: 1-recall@1\\\\n103\\\\n104\\\\n105\\\\n106\\\\nSpeed: queries per second\\\\nTested settings\\\\nPareto-optimal settings\\\\nPareto front after 50 experiments\\\\n0\\\\n1000\\\\n2000\\\\n3000\\\\n4000\\\\n5000\\\\n6000\\\\nexperiment count\\\\n0\\\\n50\\\\n100\\\\n150\\\\n200\\\\n250\\\\n300\\\\n350\\\\n400\\\\nresult count\\\\nTested settings\\\\nKept settings\\\\nFigure 1: Example of exploration of a parameter space with 3 parameters (an IndexIVFPQ with polysemous codes and HNSW coarse\\\\nquantizer, running on the Deep100M dataset).
