The benchmark generates can-\\\\ndidate index configurations to evaluate, sweeps both\\\\nconstruction-time and search-time parameters, and\\\\nmeasures these metrics.\\\\nThe accuracy metric is se-\\\\nlected as applicable, n-recall@m for k-nearest neigh-\\\\nbors, mean average precision for range search, and\\\\nmean squared error for vector codecs, and it can be\\\\nfurther customized.\\\\n5\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 6 ===\\\\nNo encoding\\\\nPQ encoding\\\\nscalar quantizer\\\\nFlat\\\\nIndexFlat\\\\nIndexPQ\\\\nIndexScalarQuantizer\\\\nIVF\\\\nIndexIVFFlat\\\\nIndexIVFPQ\\\\nIndexIVFScalarQuantizer\\\\nHNSW\\\\nIndexHSNWFlat\\\\nIndexHNSWPQ\\\\nIndexHNSWScalarQuantizer\\\\nTable 2: A few combinations of pruning approaches and compression methods. In the cells: the corresponding index implementations.\\\\nDecoupling encoding and non-exhaustive search op-\\\\ntions.\\\\nBeyond a certain scale, search time is deter-\\\\nmined by the number of distance computations be-\\\\ntween the query vector and database vectors.\\\\nThe\\\\nnon-exhaustive search methods in Faiss are either\\\\nbased on a clustering, or on a graph exploration, see\\\\nSection 5. Another limiting factor of vector search is\\\\nthe memory usage per vector (RAM or disk). In or-\\\\nder to fit more vectors, they need to be compressed.\\\\nFaiss implements a range of compression options, see\\\\nSection 4.\\\\nTherefore, Faiss indexes are built as a combination\\\\nof pruning method and a compression method, see Ta-\\\\nble 2. In the following sections, we explore the options\\\\nin these two directions.\\\\nTo evaluate a large number of index configurations\\\\nefficiently, the benchmarking framework takes advan-\\\\ntage of this compositional nature of Faiss indices dur-\\\\ning the index training and search. The training of vec-\\\\ntor transformations and k-means clustering for IVF\\\\ncoarse quantizers are factored out and reused during\\\\nthe training of compatible indices. Coarse quantizers\\\\nand IVF indices are first trained and evaluated sep-\\\\narately, the parameter space is pruned as described\\\\nin the previous section, and only the combinations\\\\nof Pareto-optimal components are benchmarked to-\\\\ngether. It is implemented in bench fw.\\\\n3.6\\\\nRefining (IndexRefine)\\\\nIt is possible to combine a fast and inaccurate in-\\\\ndexing method with a slower and more accurate\\\\nsearch\\\\n[J´egou et al., 2011b,\\\\nSubramanya et al., 2019,\\\\nGuo et al., 2020].\\\\nThis is done by querying the fast\\\\nindex to retrieve a shortlist of results. The more ac-\\\\ncurate search then computes more accurate search re-\\\\nsults only for the shortlist. This requires the accurate\\\\nindex to store the vectors in a way that allows efficient\\\\nrandom access to possibly-compressed database vec-\\\\ntors. Some implementations use a slower storage (e.g.\\\\nflash) for the second index [Subramanya et al., 2019,\\\\nSun et al., 2023b].\\\\nFor the first-level index, the relevant accuracy met-\\\\nric is the recall at the rank that will be used for re-\\\\nranking. The recall @ rank 1000 can thus sometimes\\\\nbe a relevant metric, even if the end application does\\\\nnot use the 1000th neighbor at all.\\\\nSeveral methods are also based on this refin-\\\\ning principle but do not use two separate in-\\\\ndexes.\\\\nInstead, they use two ways of interpret-\\\\ning the same compressed vectors:\\\\na fast and in-\\\\naccurate decoding and a slower but more accu-\\\\nrate decoding [Douze et al., 2016, Douze et al., 2018,\\\\nMorozov and Babenko, 2019, Amara et al., 2022] are\\\\nbased on this principle.\\\\nThe polysemous codes\\\\nmethod [Douze et al., 2016] is implemented in Faiss’s\\\\nIndexIVFPQ.\\\\n4\\\\nCompression levels\\\\nFaiss supports various vector codecs: these are meth-\\\\nods to compress vectors so that they take up less mem-\\\\nory. A compression method C : Rd →{1, ..., K}, a.k.a.\\\\na quantizer, converts a continuous multi-dimensional\\\\nvector to an integer or equivalently a fixed size bit\\\\nstring. The length of the corresponding bit string is\\\\ncalled the code size. The decoder D : {1, ..., K} →Rd\\\\nreconstructs an approximation of the vector from the\\\\ninteger. Since the number of distinct integers of a cer-\\\\ntain size is finite, the decoder can only reconstruct a\\\\nfinite number K of distinct vectors.\\\\nThe search of Equation (1) becomes approximate:\\\\nn = argmin\\\\nn=1..N\\\\n∥q −D(C(xn))∥= argmin\\\\nn=1..N\\\\n∥q −D(Cn)∥\\\\n(10)\\\\nWhere the codes Cn = C(xn) are precomputed and\\\\nstored in the index. This is the asymmetric distance\\\\ncomputation (ADC) [J´egou et al., 2010]. The symmet-\\\\nric distance computation (SDC) corresponds to the\\\\ncase when the query vector is also compressed:\\\\nn = argmin\\\\nn=1..N\\\\n∥D(C(q)) −D(Cn)∥\\\\n(11)\\\\nMost Faiss indexes perform ADC as it is more ac-\\\\ncurate: there is no accuracy loss on the query vectors.\\\\nSDC is useful when there is also a storage constraint\\\\non the queries or for indexing methods for which SDC\\\\nis faster to compute than ADC.\\\\n4.1\\\\nThe vector codecs\\\\nThe k-means vector quantizer (Kmeans)\\\\nThe ideal\\\\nvector quantizer minimizes the MSE between the orig-\\\\ninal and the decompressed vectors. This is formalized\\\\nin the Lloyd necessary conditions for the optimality of\\\\na quantizer [Lloyd, 1982].\\\\nThe k-means clustering algorithm can be seen as\\\\na quantizer that directly applies the Lloyd optimal-\\\\nity conditions [Amara et al., 2022]. The K centroids\\\\nof k-means are an explicit enumeration of all possi-\\\\nble vectors that can be reconstructed. Thus the size of\\\\nthe bit strings that the k-means quantizer produces is\\\\n⌈log2 K⌉bits.\\\\nThe k-means vector quantizer is very accurate but\\\\nthe memory usage and encoding complexity grow\\\\n6\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 7 ===\\\\nexponentially with the code size. Therefore, k-means\\\\nis impractical to use beyond 3-byte codes, correspond-\\\\ning to 16M centroids.\\\\nScalar quantizers\\\\nScalar quantizers encode each di-\\\\nmension of a vector independently.\\\\nA very classical and simple scalar quantizer is LSH\\\\n(IndexLSH), where each vector component is encoded\\\\nin a single bit by comparing it to a threshold. The\\\\nthreshold can be set to 0 or trained.\\\\nFaiss further\\\\nsupports efficient search of binary vectors via the\\\\nIndexBinary objects, see Section 4.5.\\\\nThe Faiss ScalarQuantizer also supports uniform\\\\nquantizers that encode a vector component into 8,\\\\n6 or 4 bits – referred to as SQ8, SQ6, SQ4.\\\\nA per-\\\\ncomponent scale and offset determine which values\\\\nare reconstructed. They can be set separately for each\\\\ndimension or uniformly on the whole vector.\\\\nThe\\\\nIndexRowwiseMinMax stores vectors with per-vector\\\\nnormalizing coefficients. The ranges are trained be-\\\\nforehand on a set of representative vectors. The lower-\\\\nprecision float16 representation is also considered as a\\\\nscalar quantizer, SQfp16.\\\\nMulti-codebook quantizers.\\\\nFaiss contains several\\\\nmulti-codebook quantization options. They are built\\\\nfrom M vector quantizers that can reconstruct K dis-\\\\ntinct values each. The codes produced by these meth-\\\\nods are of the form (c1, ..., cM) ∈{1, ..., K}M, i.e. each\\\\ncode indexes one of the quantizers. The number of re-\\\\nconstructed vectors is KM and the code size is thus\\\\nM⌈log2(K)⌉.\\\\nThe product quantizer (ProductQuantizer, also\\\\nnoted PQ) is a simple multi-codebook quantizer that\\\\nsplits the input vector into M sub-vectors and quan-\\\\ntizes them separately [J´egou et al., 2010] with a k-\\\\nmeans quantizer. At reconstruction time, the individ-\\\\nual reconstructions are concatenated to produce the fi-\\\\nnal code. In the following, we will use the notation\\\\nPQ6x10 for a product quantizer with 6 sub-vectors\\\\neach encoded in 10 bits (M = 6, K = 210).\\\\nAdditive quantizers are a family of multi-codebook\\\\nquantizers\\\\nwhere\\\\nthe\\\\nreconstructions\\\\nfrom\\\\nsub-\\\\nquantizers are summed up together. Finding the opti-\\\\nmal encoding for a vector given the codebooks is NP-\\\\nhard, so practical additive quantizers are heuristics to\\\\nfind near-optimal codes.\\\\nFaiss supports two types of additive quantiz-\\\\ners.\\\\nThe residual quantizer (ResidualQuantizer)\\\\nproceeds\\\\nsequentially,\\\\nby\\\\nencoding\\\\nthe\\\\ndiffer-\\\\nence (residual) of the vector to encode and the\\\\none that is reconstructed by the previous sub-\\\\nquantizers [Chen et al., 2010].\\\\nThe local\\\\nsearch\\\\nquantizer\\\\n(LocalSearchQuantizer)\\\\nstarts\\\\nfrom\\\\na\\\\nsub-optimal encoding of the vector and locally ex-\\\\nplores neighbording codes in a simulated annealing\\\\nprocess [Martinez et al., 2016, Martinez et al., 2018].\\\\nWe use notations LSQ6x10 and RQ6x10 to refer to\\\\nadditive quantizers with 6 codebooks of size 210.\\\\nAdditive quantizer\\\\nProduct quantizer\\\\nScalar quantizer\\\\nBinarization\\\\nVector quantizer\\\\nProduct - additive quantizer\\\\nFigure 2: The hierarchy of quantizers. Each quantizer can represent\\\\nthe set of reproduction values of the enclosed quantizers.\\\\nFaiss also supports a combination of PQ and\\\\nresidual quantizer, ProductResidualQuantizer.\\\\nIn\\\\nthat case, the vector is split in sub-vectors that\\\\nare encoded independently with additive quantiz-\\\\ners [Babenko and Lempitsky, 2015]. The codes from\\\\nthe sub-quantizers are concatenated. We use the no-\\\\ntation PRQ2x6x10 to indicate that vectors are split in\\\\n2 and encoded independently with RQ6x10, yielding\\\\na total of 12 codebooks of size 210.\\\\nHierarchy of quantizers\\\\nAlthough this is not by de-\\\\nsign, it turns out that there is a strict ordering be-\\\\ntween the quantizers described before. This means\\\\nthat quantizer i+1 can have the same set of reproduc-\\\\ntion values as quantizer i: it is more flexible and more\\\\ndata adaptive. The hierarchy of quantizers is shown\\\\nin Figure 2:\\\\n1. the binary representation with bits +1 and -1 can\\\\nbe represented as a scalar quantizer with 1 bit per\\\\ncomponent;\\\\n2. the scalar quantizer can be represented as a prod-\\\\nuct quantizer with 1 dimension per sub-vector\\\\nand uniform per-dimension quantizer;\\\\n3. the product quantizer can be represented as a\\\\nproduct-additive quantizer where the additive\\\\nquantizer has a single level;\\\\n4. the product additive quantizer is an addi-\\\\ntive quantizer where within each codebook all\\\\ncomponents outside one sub-vector are set to\\\\n0 [Babenko and Lempitsky, 2014];\\\\n5. the additive quantizer (and any other quantizer)\\\\ncan be represented as a vector quantizer where\\\\nthe codebook entries are the explicit enumeration\\\\nof all possible reconstructions.\\\\nThe implications of this hierarchy are (1) the de-\\\\ngrees of freedom for the reproduction values of quan-\\\\ntizer i + 1 are larger than for i, so it is more accurate\\\\n(2) quantizer i+1 has a higher capacity so it consumes\\\\nmore resources in terms of training time and storage\\\\noverhead than i. In practice, the product quantizer of-\\\\nten offers a good tradeoff, which explains its adoption.\\\\n7\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 8 ===\\\\n0.16\\\\n0.18\\\\n0.20\\\\n0.22\\\\n0.24\\\\n0.26\\\\n0.28\\\\n0.30\\\\n0.32\\\\nMSE\\\\n101\\\\n102\\\\nencoding time (s for 1M vectors, 32 threads)\\\\n 1\\\\n 2\\\\n 4\\\\n 8\\\\n 16\\\\n 32\\\\nDeep1M encoded to \\\\n 8 bytes per vector\\\\n(P)RQ\\\\n(P)RQ with LUT\\\\n(P)LSQ\\\\n(P)LSQ on GPU\\\\n10x6\\\\n5x12\\\\n6x10\\\\n8x8\\\\n2x2x12\\\\n2x3x10\\\\n2x4x8\\\\n2x5x6\\\\n3x2x10\\\\n0.80\\\\n0.85\\\\n0.90\\\\n0.95\\\\n1.00\\\\n1.05\\\\n1.10\\\\nMSE\\\\n102\\\\n103\\\\nencoding time (s for 1M vectors, 32 threads)\\\\n 1\\\\n 2\\\\n 4\\\\n 8\\\\n 16\\\\n 32\\\\nContriever1M encoded to \\\\n 64 bytes per vector\\\\n(P)RQ\\\\n(P)RQ with LUT\\\\n(P)LSQ\\\\n(P)LSQ on GPU\\\\n42x12\\\\n51x10\\\\n64x8\\\\n2x21x12\\\\n2x25x10\\\\n2x32x8\\\\n3x14x12\\\\n3x17x10\\\\n4x10x12\\\\n4x12x10\\\\nFigure 3: Comparison of additive quantizers in terms of encoding time vs. accuracy (MSE). Many of these transformations are d-\\\\ndimensional rotations, that do not change comparison\\\\nmetrics like cosine, L2 and inner product.\\\\nScalar quantizers assign the same number of bits\\\\nper vector component. However, for distance com-\\\\nparisons, if specific vector components have a higher\\\\nvariance, they have more impact on the distances. In\\\\nother works, a variable number of bits are assigned\\\\nper component [Sandhawalia and J´egou, 2010]. How-\\\\never, it is simpler to apply a random rotation to\\\\nthe input vectors, which in Faiss can be done with\\\\na RandomRotationMatrix.\\\\nThe random rotation\\\\nspreads the variance over all the dimensions without\\\\nchanging the measured distances.\\\\nAn important transform is the Principal Compo-\\\\nnent Analysis (PCA), that reduces the number of di-\\\\nmensions d of the input vectors to a user-specified\\\\nd′. It amounts to projecting the vectors\\\\non a random direction [Datar et al., 2004].\\\\nThe off-\\\\nsets on that direction are then discretized into buckets\\\\nwhere the database vectors are stored. At search time,\\\\nthe buckets nearest to the query vector’s projection are\\\\nvisited. In practice, several projection directions are\\\\nneeded to make it accurate, at the cost of search time.\\\\nA fundamental drawback of this method is that it is\\\\nnot data-adaptive, although some improvements are\\\\npossible [Paulev´e et al., 2010].\\\\nAn alternative way of pruning the search space is\\\\nto use tree-based indexing. In that case, the dataset is\\\\nstored in the leaves of a tree [Muja and Lowe, 2014].\\\\nWhen querying a vector, the search starts at the root\\\\nnode. If they are unbalanced,\\\\nthe number of distances computed for a given PIVF\\\\nincreases with the imbalance factor.\\\\nThe imbalance is mainly due to high-norm cen-\\\\ntroids that attract the database vectors in their clus-\\\\nters. To avoid this, we can normalize the centroids at\\\\neach iteration.\\\\nFigure 7 shows that for the contriever MIPS dataset,\\\\nthe imbalance factor is quite high. This appears\\\\nfor applications such as large-scale data deduplica-\\\\ntion. In this case, rather than loading an entire index\\\\nin memory and processing queries one small batch\\\\nat a time, it can be more memory-efficient to load\\\\nonly the quantizer, quantize the queries, and then it-\\\\nerate over the index by loading it one chunk at a\\\\ntime. Big-batch search is implemented in the module\\\\ncontrib.big batch search.\\\\n5.2\\\\nGraph based\\\\nGraph-based indexing consists in building a directed\\\\ngraph whose nodes are the vectors to index. At search\\\\ntime, the graph is explored by following the edges to-\\\\nwards the nodes that are closest to the query vector.\\\\nIn practice, the search is not greedy but maintains a\\\\npriority queue with the most promising edges to ex-\\\\nplore. Thus, the tradeoff at search time is given by the\\\\nnumber of exploration steps: higher is more accurate\\\\nbut slower.\\\\nA graph-based algorithm is a general framework\\\\nin fact.\\\\nTree-based search or IVF can be seen as\\\\nspecial cases of graphs.\\\\nGraphs can be seen as a\\\\nway to precompute neighbors for the database vec-\\\\ntors, then match the query to one of the vertices\\\\nand follow the neighbors from there.\\\\nHowever,\\\\nthey can also be built to handle out-of-distribution\\\\nqueries [Jaiswal et al., 2022].\\\\nGiven the search algorithm, taking a pure k-nearest\\\\nneighbor graph is not optimal because the greedy\\\\nsearch is prone to finding local minima. Therefore, the\\\\ngraph building heuristic consists in balancing edges\\\\nto nearest neighbors and edges that reach more dis-\\\\ntant nodes. Most graph methods fix the number of\\\\noutgoing edges per node, which adjusts the tradeoff\\\\n0.70\\\\n0.75\\\\n0.80\\\\n0.85\\\\n0.90\\\\n0.95\\\\n1.00\\\\n1-recall@1\\\\n104\\\\n105\\\\n106\\\\nQueries per second\\\\n64 \\\\n128 \\\\n256 \\\\n512 \\\\n1024 \\\\n64 \\\\n128 \\\\n256 \\\\n512 \\\\n1024 \\\\n2048 \\\\n8 edges\\\\n16 edges\\\\n32 edges\\\\n64 edges\\\\nFigure 8: Comparison of graph-based indexing methods HNSW\\\\n(full lines) and NSG (dashes) to index Deep1M. We sweep the trade-\\\\noffs between speed and accuracy by varying the number of graph\\\\ntraversal steps (indicated for some of the curves).\\\\nbetween search speed and memory usage. The mem-\\\\nory usage per vector breaks down into (1) the possibly\\\\ncompressed vector and (2) the outgoing edges for that\\\\nvector [Douze et al., 2018].\\\\nFaiss implements two graph-based algorithms:\\\\nHNSW and NSG, in the IndexHNSW and IndexNSG\\\\nclasses, respectively.\\\\nHNSW\\\\nThe hierarchical navigable small world\\\\ngraph [Malkov and Yashunin, 2018] is an elegant\\\\nsearch structure where some vertices (nodes), selected\\\\nrandomly, are promoted to be hubs that are explored\\\\nfirst. One of the attractive properties of HNSW is that\\\\nit is built incrementally. As a consequence, vectors can\\\\nbe added to it on-the-fly.\\\\nNSG\\\\nThe\\\\nNavigating\\\\nSpreading-out\\\\nGraph [Fu et al., 2017] is built from a k-nearest\\\\nneighbor graph that must be provided on input. At\\\\nbuilding time, some short-range edges are replaced\\\\nwith longer-range edges. The input k-nn graph can\\\\nbe built with a brute force algorithm or with a special-\\\\nized method such as NN-descent [Dong et al., 2011]\\\\n(NNDescent). Unlike HNSW, NSG does not rely on\\\\nmulti-layer graph structures, but uses long connec-\\\\ntions to achieve fast navigation.\\\\nIn addition, NSG\\\\nstarts from a fixed center point when searching.\\\\nDiscussion\\\\nFigure 8 compares the speed vs.\\\\nac-\\\\ncuracy for the NSG and HNSW indexes. The main\\\\nbuild-time hyper-parameter of the two methods is the\\\\nnumber of edges per node, so we tested several set-\\\\ntings (for HNSW this is the number of edges on the\\\\nbase level of the hierachical graph). The main search-\\\\ntime parameter is the number of graph traversal steps\\\\nduring search (parameter efSearch for HNSW and\\\\nsearch L for NSG), which we vary to plot each curve.\\\\nIncreasing the number of edges improves the results\\\\nonly to some extent: beyond 64 edges it degrades.\\\\n12\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 13 ===\\\\nNSG obtains better tradeoffs in general, at the cost of\\\\na longer build time. Building the input k-NN graph\\\\nwith NN-descent for 1M vectors takes 37 s, and about\\\\nthe same time with brute force search on a GPU (but\\\\nin that case the k-NN graph is exact). The NSG graph\\\\nis frozen after the first batch of vectors is added, there\\\\nis no easy way to add more vectors afterwards.\\\\nIVF vs. graph-based.\\\\nAn IVF index can be seen as\\\\na special case of graph-based index, especially if a\\\\nsmall graph-based index is used as coarse quantizer.\\\\nIn Faiss, graph-based indices are a good option for in-\\\\ndexes where there is no constraint on memory usage,\\\\ntypically for indexes below 1M vectors. Beyond 10M\\\\nvectors, the construction time typically becomes the\\\\nlimiting factor. For larger indexes, where compression\\\\nis required to even fit the database vectors in memory,\\\\nIVF indexes are the only option. However, as shown\\\\nin Section 5.1, the optimal number of centroids is so\\\\nlarge that a graph-based index should be used to per-\\\\nform the coarse quantization, and much of the search\\\\ntime is spent in the coarse quantization.\\\\n6\\\\nDatabase operations\\\\nIn all the experiments above, the indexes are built\\\\nin one go with all the vectors, while search oper-\\\\nations are performed with one batch containing all\\\\nquery vectors. In real settings, the index evolves over\\\\ntime, vectors may be dynamically added or removed,\\\\nsearches may have to take into account metadata, etc.\\\\nIn this section we show how Faiss supports these\\\\noperations to some extent, mainly on IVF indexes.\\\\nWhen more fine-grained control is required, there are\\\\nspecific APIs to interface with external storage (Sec-\\\\ntion 7.4).\\\\n6.1\\\\nIdentifier-based operations\\\\nFaiss indexes support two types of identifiers: sequen-\\\\ntial ids are based on the order of additions in the in-\\\\ndex. On the other hand, the user can provide arbi-\\\\ntrary 63-bit integer ids along with each vector. The\\\\ncorresponding addition methods for the index are add\\\\nand add with ids. In addition, Faiss supports remov-\\\\ning vectors (remove ids) and updating vector them\\\\n(update vectors) by passing the corresponding ids.\\\\nUnlike e.g. Usearch [Vardanian, 2022], Faiss does\\\\nnot store arbitrary metadata with the vectors, only 63-\\\\nbit integer ids can be used (the sign bit is reserved for\\\\ninvalid results).\\\\nFlat indexes.\\\\nSequential indexes (IndexFlatCodes)\\\\nstore vectors as a flat array. They support only se-\\\\nquential ids. When arbitrary ids are needed, the index\\\\ncan be embedded in a IndexIDMap, that translates se-\\\\nquence numbers to arbitrary ids using a int64 array.\\\\nThis enables add with ids and returns the arbitrary\\\\nids at search time. To also perform id-based opera-\\\\ntions, a more powerful wrapper class, IndexIDMap2,\\\\nuses a hash table that maps arbitrary ids back to the\\\\nsequential ids.\\\\nSince\\\\ngraph\\\\nindexes\\\\nrely\\\\non\\\\nan\\\\nembedded\\\\nIndexFlatCodes to store the actual vectors, they\\\\nshould also be wrapped with the mapping classes.\\\\nNote however that HNSW does not support sup-\\\\npression and mutation, and that NSG does not even\\\\nsupport adding vectors incrementally.\\\\nSupporting\\\\nthis requires heuristics to re-build the graph when\\\\nit is mutated, which are implemented in HNSWlib\\\\nand [Singh et al., 2021] but could be suboptimal\\\\nindexing-wise.\\\\nIVF indexes.\\\\nThe IVF indexing structure does sup-\\\\nports user-provided ids natively at addition and\\\\nsearch time. However, id-based access may require\\\\na sequential scan, since the entries are stored in an ar-\\\\nbitrary order in the inverted lists. Therefore, the IVF\\\\nindex can optionally maintain a DirectMap, that maps\\\\nuser-visible ids to the inverted list and the offset they\\\\nare stored in. The map can be an array, which is ap-\\\\npropriate for sequential ids, or a hash table, for ar-\\\\nbitrary 63-bit ids. Obviously, the direct map incurs\\\\na memory overhead and an add-time computation\\\\noverhead, therefore it is disabled by default. When\\\\nthe direct map is enabled, lookup, removal and up-\\\\ndate are supported.\\\\n6.2\\\\nFiltered search\\\\nVector filtering consists in returning only database\\\\nvectors based on some search-time criterion, other\\\\nvectors are ignored. Faiss has basic support for vector\\\\nfiltering: the user can provide a predicate (IDSelector\\\\ncallback), and if the predicate returns false on the vec-\\\\ntor id, the vector is ignored.\\\\nTherefore, if metadata is needed to filter the vec-\\\\ntors, the callback function needs to do an indirection\\\\nto the metadata table, which is inefficient. Another\\\\napproach is to exploit the unused bits of the identi-\\\\nfier. If n documents are indexed with sequential ids,\\\\n63 −⌈log2(N)⌉bits are unused.\\\\nThis is sufficient to store enumerated types (e.g. .\\\\ncountry codes, music genres, license types, etc.), dates\\\\n(as days since some origin), version numbers, etc.\\\\nHowever, it is insufficient for more complex metadata.\\\\nIn the example use case below, we use the available\\\\nbits to implement a more complex filtering method.\\\\nFiltering with bag-of-word vectors.\\\\n4\\\\nEach query\\\\nand database vector has is associated with a few terms\\\\nfrom a fixed vocabulary of size v (for the queries there\\\\nare only 1 or 2 words). The filtering consists in con-\\\\nsidering only the database vectors that include all the\\\\nquery terms. This metadata is given as a sparse matrix\\\\nMmeta ∈{0, 1}N×v.\\\\nThe basic implementation of the filter uses query\\\\nvector q and the associated words w1, w2 ∈{1...v}.\\\\n4This example is from the the BigANN’23 challenge, https://\\\\nbig-ann-benchmarks.com/neurips23.html.\\\\n13\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 14 ===\\\\nBefore computing a distance to a vector with id i, it\\\\nfetches row i of Mmeta to verify that w1 and w2 are\\\\nin it. This predicate is relatively slow because (1) it\\\\nrequires to access Mmeta, which causes cache misses\\\\nand (2) it performs an iterative binary search. Since\\\\nthe callback is called in the tightest inner loop of the\\\\nsearch function, and since the IVF search tends to per-\\\\nform many vector comparisons, this has non negligi-\\\\nble performance impact.\\\\nTo speed up this test, we can use a nifty piece of\\\\nbit manipulation. In this example, N = 107, so we\\\\nuse only ⌈log2 N⌉= 24 bits of the ids, leaving 63 −\\\\n24 = 39 bits that are always 0. We associate to each\\\\nword j a 39-bit signature S[j], and the to each set of\\\\nwords the binary “or” of these signatures. The query\\\\nis represented by sq = S[w1] ∨S[w2]. Database entry\\\\ni with words Wi is represented by si = ∨w∈WiS[w].\\\\nThen we have the following implication: if {w1, w2} ⊂\\\\nWi then all 1 bits of sq are also set to 1 in si:\\\\n{w1, w2} ⊂Wi ⇒¬si ∧sq = 0\\\\n(19)\\\\nwhich is equivalent to:\\\\n¬si ∧sq ̸= 0 ⇒{w1, w2} ̸⊂Wi\\\\n(20)\\\\nThis binary test is very cheap to perform: a few ma-\\\\nchine instructions on data that is already in machine\\\\nregisters. It can thus be used as a pre-filter to apply\\\\nthe full membership test on candidates.\\\\nThe remaining degree of freedom is how to choose\\\\nthe binary signatures, because this rule is always\\\\nvalid, but its filtering ability depends on the choice of\\\\nthe signatures S. We experimented with iid Bernouilli\\\\nbits with varying p.\\\\np= probability of 1\\\\n0.05\\\\n0.1\\\\n0.2\\\\n0.5\\\\nFilter hit rate\\\\n75.4%\\\\n82.1%\\\\n76.4%\\\\n42.0%\\\\ni.e. the best setting avoids to do the full check more\\\\nthan 4/5th of the times.\\\\nPre- or post-filtering.\\\\nThere are two possible ap-\\\\nproaches to filtered search: post-filtering, which is de-\\\\nscribed above, and pre-filtering, where only vectors\\\\nwith appropriate metadata are considered in vector\\\\nsearch. The pre-filtering generates a subset of vectors\\\\nto compare with.\\\\nTherefore, the decision to use pre- or post-filtering\\\\ndepends on whether the subset of vectors is large or\\\\nnot. This can be estimated prior to the search depend-\\\\ning on the filtering ability of the query metadata.\\\\nIn the bag-of-words example, pre-filtering can ex-\\\\nploit a term-based inverted file, which is the Mmeta\\\\nrepresented in compressed sparse column format. The\\\\nproduct of the frequencies of w1 and w2 is an estimate\\\\nof what fraction of vectors pre-filtering will perform.\\\\n7\\\\nFaiss engineering\\\\nFaiss started in a research environment. As a conse-\\\\nquence, it grew organically, one index at a time, as\\\\nIndex implementations\\\\nIndexIVFPQ, IndexFlat, etc.\\\\nGPU index implementations\\\\nGpuIndexIVFPQ, …\\\\nCUDA library\\\\nBLAS library \\\\n(MKL, openblas)\\\\nUtilities and primitives\\\\nHeap, ProductQuantizer, Clustering …\\\\nSWIG wrapper (Python)\\\\nswigfaiss.swig → swigfaiss.py\\\\nAdaptor layer \\\\n__init__.py, class_enhancement.py\\\\nC wrapper \\\\nPython contrib library\\\\n(contrib.datasets, etc.)\\\\nRust / C#  code\\\\nC++ code \\\\ndemos /  tests \\\\nPython code \\\\ntests / benchs\\\\nNumpy library\\\\nRust wrapper \\\\nC# wrapper,...\\\\nFaiss\\\\nC++/cuda\\\\n cppcontrib library\\\\n(SADecodeKernels...)\\\\nFigure 9: Architecture of the Faiss library. Arrows indicate depen-\\\\ndencies. At the bottom are the library’s dependencies, at the top are\\\\nexample software that depends on Faiss, most notably its extensive\\\\ntest suite.\\\\nindexing research was making progress. In the fol-\\\\nlowing, we briefly mention the guiding principles that\\\\nkept the library coherent, how optimization is per-\\\\nformed and an example of how Faiss internals are ex-\\\\nposed so that it can be embedded in a vector database.\\\\n7.1\\\\nCode structure\\\\nThe core of Faiss is implemented in C++. The guiding\\\\nprinciples are (1) the code should be as open as pos-\\\\nsible, so that users can access all the implementation\\\\ndetails of the indexes; (2) Faiss should be easy to em-\\\\nbed from external libraries; (3) the core library focuses\\\\non vector search only.\\\\nTherefore, all fields of the classes are public (C++\\\\nstruct). Faiss is a late adopter for C++ standards, so\\\\nthat it can be used with relatively old compilers (cur-\\\\nrently C++17).\\\\nFaiss’s basic data types are concrete (not templates):\\\\nvectors are always represented as 32-bit floats that are\\\\nportable and provide a good tradeoff between size\\\\nand accuracy. Similarly, all vector ids are represented\\\\nwith 64-bit integers. This is often larger than neces-\\\\nsary for sequential numbering but is widely used for\\\\ndatabase identifiers.\\\\n7.2\\\\nHigh-level interface\\\\nFigure 9 shows the structure of the library. The C++\\\\ncore library and the GPU add-on have as few depen-\\\\ndencies as possible: only a BLAS implementation and\\\\nCUDA itself.\\\\nIn order to facilitate experimentation, the whole\\\\nlibrary is wrapped for scripting languages such as\\\\nPython with numpy.\\\\nTo this end, SWIG5 exhaus-\\\\ntively generates wrappers for all C++ classes, methods\\\\nand variables. The associated Python layer also con-\\\\ntains benchmarking code, dataset definitions, driver\\\\ncode. More and more functionality is embedded in\\\\n5https://www.swig.org/\\\\n14\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 15 ===\\\\nthe contrib package of Faiss. Faiss also provides a\\\\npure C API, which is useful for producing bindings\\\\nfor programming languages such as Rust or Java.\\\\nThe Index is presented to the end user as a mono-\\\\nlithic object, even when it embeds other indexes\\\\nas quantizers, refinement indexes or sharded sub-\\\\nindexes.\\\\nTherefore, an index can be duplicated\\\\nwith clone index and serialized into as a single byte\\\\nstream using a single function, write index. It also\\\\ncontains the necessary headers so that it can be read\\\\nby a generic function, read index.\\\\nIndex objects can be instantiated explicitly in C++\\\\nor Python, but it is more common to build them\\\\nwith the index factory function.\\\\nThis function\\\\ntakes a string that describes the index structure\\\\nand its main parameters.\\\\nFor example, the string\\\\nPCA160,IVF20000_HNSW,PQ20x10,RFlat instan-\\\\ntiates an IVF index with KIVF = 20000, where the\\\\ncoarse quantizer is a HNSW index; then the vectors\\\\nare represented with a PQ20x10 product quantizer.\\\\nThe data is preprocessed with a PCA to 160 dimen-\\\\nsions, and the search results are re-ranked with a re-\\\\nfinement index that performs exact distance computa-\\\\ntions. All the index parameters are set to reasonable\\\\ndefaults, e.g. the PQ encodes the residual of the vec-\\\\ntors w.r.t. the coarse quantization centroids.\\\\nFaiss provides dedicated standalone vector codec\\\\nfunctions sa encode, sa decode and sa code size as\\\\na part of Index API.\\\\n7.3\\\\nOptimization\\\\nApproach to optimization.\\\\nFaiss aims at being fea-\\\\nture complete first. A non-optimal version of all in-\\\\ndexes is implemented first. Code is optimized only\\\\nwhen it appears that runtime is important for a cer-\\\\ntain index. The non-optimized setting is used to con-\\\\ntrol the correctness of the optimized version.\\\\nOften, only a subset of data sizes are optimized. For\\\\nexample, for PQ indexes, only K = 28 and K = 24\\\\nand d/M ∈{2, 4, 8, 16, 20} are fully optimized. For\\\\nIndexLSH search, only code sizes 4, 8, 16, 20 are opti-\\\\nmized. Fixing these sizes allows to write “kernels”, se-\\\\nquences of instructions without explicit loops or tests,\\\\nthat aim to maximize arithmetic throughput.\\\\nWhen generic scalar CPU optimizations are ex-\\\\nhausted, Faiss also optimizes specifically for some\\\\nhardware platforms.\\\\nCPU vectorization.\\\\nModern CPUs support Single\\\\nInstruction, Multiple Data (SIMD) operations, specif-\\\\nically AVX/AVX2 for x86 and NEON for ARM. Faiss\\\\nexploits those at three levels.\\\\nWhen operations are simple enough (e.g. element-\\\\nwise vector sum), the code is written in a way that the\\\\ncompiler can vectorize the code by itself, which often\\\\nboils down to adding restrict keywords to signal\\\\nthat arrays are not overlapping.\\\\nThe second level leverages SIMD variables and in-\\\\nstructions through C++ compiler extensions.\\\\nFaiss\\\\nincludes simdlib, a collection of classes intended as\\\\na layer above the AVX and NEON instruction sets.\\\\nHowever, much of the SIMD is done specifically for\\\\none instruction set – most often AVX – because it is\\\\nmore efficient.\\\\nThe third level of optimization is to adapt the\\\\ndata layout and algorithms in order to speed up\\\\ntheir SIMD implementation.\\\\nThe 4-bit product\\\\nand additive quantizer implementations are imple-\\\\nmented in this way, inspired by the SCANN li-\\\\nbrary [Guo et al., 2020]: the layout of the PQ codes\\\\nfor several consecutive vectors is interleaved in mem-\\\\nory so that a vector permutation can be used to\\\\nperform the LUT lookups of Equation (14) in par-\\\\nallel.\\\\nThis is implemented in the FastScan vari-\\\\nants of PQ and AQ indexes (IndexPQFastScan,\\\\nIndexIVFResidualQuantizerFastScan, etc.).\\\\nGPU Faiss.\\\\nPorting Faiss to the GPU is an involved\\\\nundertaking due to substantial architectural specifici-\\\\nties. The implementation of GPU Faiss is detailed in\\\\n[Johnson et al., 2019], we summarize the GPU imple-\\\\nmentation challenges therein.\\\\nModern multi-core CPUs are highly latency opti-\\\\nmized:\\\\nthey employ an extensive cache hierarchy,\\\\nbranch prediction, speculative execution and out-of-\\\\norder code execution to improve serial program exe-\\\\ncution. In contrast, GPUs have a limited cache hier-\\\\narchy and omit many of these latency optimizations.\\\\nThey instead possess a larger number of concurrent\\\\nthreads of execution (Nvidia’s A100 GPU allows for\\\\nup to 6,912 warps, each roughly equivalent to a 32-\\\\nwide vector SIMD CPU thread of execution), a large\\\\nnumber of floating-point and integer arithmetic func-\\\\ntional units (A100 has up to 19.5 teraflops per sec-\\\\nond of fp32 fused-multiply add throughput), and a\\\\nmassive register set to allow for a high number of\\\\nlong latency pending instructions in flight (A100 has\\\\n27 MiB of register memory).\\\\nThey are thus largely\\\\nthroughput-optimized machines.\\\\nThe algorithmic techniques used in vector search\\\\ncan be grouped into three broad categories:\\\\ndis-\\\\ntance computation of floating-point or binary vectors\\\\n(which may have been produced via dequantization\\\\nfrom a compressed form), table lookups (as seen in\\\\nPQ distance computations) or scanning (as seen when\\\\ntraversing IVF lists), and irregular, sequential compu-\\\\ntations such as linked-list traversal (as used in graph-\\\\nbased indices) or ranking the k closest vectors.\\\\nDistance computation is easy on GPUs and read-\\\\nily exceeds CPU performance, as GPUs are optimized\\\\nfor matrix-matrix multiplication such as that seen in\\\\nIndexFlat or IVFFlat. Table lookups and list scan-\\\\nning can also be made performant on GPUs, as it is\\\\npossible to stage small tables (as seen in product quan-\\\\ntization) in shared memory (roughly a user-controlled\\\\nL1 cache) or register memory and perform lookups in\\\\nparallel across all warps.\\\\nSequential table scanning in IVF indices requires\\\\nloading data from main (global) memory. While laten-\\\\n15\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 16 ===\\\\ncies to access main memory are high, for table scan-\\\\nning we know in advance what data we wish to ac-\\\\ncess, so the data movement from main memory into\\\\nregisters can be pipelined or use double buffering, so\\\\nwe can achieve close to peak possible performance.\\\\nSelecting the k closest vectors to a query vector by\\\\nranking distances on the CPU is best implemented\\\\nwith a min- or max-heap. On the GPU, the sequential\\\\noperations involved in heap operations would simi-\\\\nlarly force the GPU into a latency-bound regime. This\\\\nis the largest challenge for GPU implementation of\\\\nvector search, as the time needed for the heap im-\\\\nplementation an order of magnitude greater than all\\\\nother arithmetic. To handle this, we developed an effi-\\\\ncient GPU k-selection algorithm [Johnson et al., 2019]\\\\nthat allows for ranking candidate vectors in a single\\\\npass, operating at a substantial fraction of peak pos-\\\\nsible performance per memory bandwidth limits. It\\\\nrelies upon heavy usage of the high-speed, large reg-\\\\nister memory on GPUs, and small-set bitonic sorting\\\\nvia warp shuffles with buffering techniques.\\\\nIrregular computations such as walking graph\\\\nstructures for graph-based indices like HNSW tend\\\\nto remain in the latency-bound (due to the sequen-\\\\ntial traversal) rather than arithmetic throughput or\\\\nmemory bandwidth-bound regimes. Here, GPUs are\\\\nat a disadvantage as compared to CPUs, and emerg-\\\\ning techniques such as CAGRA [Ootomo et al., 2023]\\\\nare required to parallelize otherwise sequential oper-\\\\nations with graph traversal.\\\\nGPU Faiss implements brute-force GpuIndexFlat\\\\nas\\\\nwell\\\\nas\\\\nthe\\\\nIVF\\\\nindices\\\\nGpuIndexIVFFlat,\\\\nGpuIndexIVFScalarQuantizer and GpuIndexIVFPQ,\\\\nwhich are the most useful for large-scale indexing.\\\\nThe coarse quantizer for the IVF indices can be on\\\\neither CPU or GPU. The GPU index objects have\\\\nthe same interface as their CPU counterparts and\\\\nthe functions index cpu to gpu / index gpu to cpu\\\\nconvert between them.\\\\nMultiple GPUs are also\\\\nsupported. GPU indexes can take inputs and outputs\\\\nin GPU or CPU memory as input and output, and\\\\nPython interface can handle Pytorch tensors.\\\\nAdvanced options for Faiss components and indices\\\\nMany Faiss components expose internal parameters\\\\nto fine-tune the tradeoff between metrics: number of\\\\niterations of k-means, batch sizes for brute-force dis-\\\\ntance computations, etc.\\\\nDefault parameter values\\\\nwere chosen to work reasonably well in most cases.\\\\nMulti-threading\\\\nFaiss relies on OpenMP to handle\\\\nmulti-threading. By default, Faiss switches to multi-\\\\nthreading processing if it is beneficial, for example,\\\\nat training and batch addition time.\\\\nFaiss multi-\\\\nthreading behavior may be controlled with standard\\\\nOpenMP environment variables and functions, such\\\\nas omp set num threads.\\\\nWhen searching a single vector, Faiss does not\\\\nspawn multiple threads.\\\\nHowever, when batched\\\\nqueries are provided, Faiss processes them in par-\\\\nallel, exploiting the effectiveness of the CPU cache\\\\nand batched linear algebra operations. This is faster\\\\nthan calling search from multiple threads. Therefore,\\\\nqueries should be submitted by batches if possible.\\\\n7.4\\\\nInterfacing with external storage\\\\nFaiss indexes are based on simple storage classes,\\\\nmainly std::vector to make copy-construction eas-\\\\nier. The default implementation of IndexIVF is based\\\\non this storage.\\\\nHowever, to give vector database\\\\ndevelopers more control over the storage of inverted\\\\nlists, Faiss provides two lower-level APIs.\\\\nArbitrary inverted lists.\\\\nThe IVF index uses an\\\\nabstract InvertedLists object as its storage.\\\\nThe\\\\nobject exposes routines to read one inverted list,\\\\nadd entries to it and remove entries.\\\\nThe default\\\\nArrayInvertedLists uses in-memory storage.\\\\nAl-\\\\nternatively, OnDiskInvertedLists provides memory-\\\\nmapped storage.\\\\nMore complex implementations can access a key-\\\\nvalue storage either by storing the entire inverted list\\\\nas a value, or by utilizing key prefix scan operations\\\\nlike the one supported by RocksDB to treat multiple\\\\nkeys prefixed by the same identifier as one inverted\\\\nlist. To this end, the InvertedLists implementation\\\\nexposes an InvertedListsIterator and fetches the\\\\ncodes and ids from the underlying key-value store,\\\\nwhich usually exposes a similar iterable interface.\\\\nAdding, updating and removing codes can be dele-\\\\ngated to the underlying key-value store. We provide\\\\nan implementation for RocksDB in rocksdb ivf.\\\\nScanner objects.\\\\nWith the abstraction above, the\\\\nscanning loop is still controlled by Faiss. If the call-\\\\ning code needs to control the looping code, then the\\\\nFaiss IVF index provides an InvertedListScanner\\\\nobject.\\\\nThe scanner’s state includes the current\\\\nquery vector and current inverted list. It provides a\\\\ndistance to code method that, given a code, com-\\\\nputes the distance from the query to the decom-\\\\npressed vector. At a slightly higher level, it loops over\\\\na set of codes and updates a provided result buffer.\\\\nThis abstraction is useful when the inverted lists\\\\nare not stored sequentially or fragmented into sub-\\\\nlists because of metadata filtering [Huang et al., 2020].\\\\nFaiss is used only to perform the coarse quantization\\\\nand the vector encoding.\\\\n8\\\\nFaiss applications\\\\nFaiss is used in many configurations. Hundreds of\\\\nvector search applications rely on it, both within Meta\\\\nand externally. Below we present a few use cases that\\\\nshowcase either an extreme scale or an application\\\\nwith particular impact.\\\\n16\\\\n\\\\n\\\\n=== PDF page 17 ===\\\\n8.1\\\\nTrillion scale index\\\\nFor this example, Faiss is used to index 1.5 trillion vec-\\\\ntors in 144 dimensions. The indexing needs to be ac-\\\\ncurate, therefore the compression of the vectors is lim-\\\\nited to 54 bytes with a PCA to 72 dimensions and 6-bit\\\\nscalar quantizer (PCAR72,SQ6).\\\\nA HNSW coarse quantizer with 10M centroids is\\\\nused for the IndexIVFScalarQuantizer, trained with\\\\na simple distributed GPU k-means (implemented in\\\\nfaiss.clustering).\\\\nAfter the training is finished, the index is built in 3\\\\nphases:\\\\n1. shard over ids: add the input vectors in 2000\\\\nshards independently, producing 2000 indexes\\\\n(that fit in RAM);\\\\n2. shard over lists:\\\\nbuild the 100 indexes corre-\\\\nsponding each to a subset of 100k inverted lists.\\\\nThis is done on 100 different machines, each ac-\\\\ncessing the 2000 sharded indices, and writing the\\\\nresults directly to a shared disk partition;\\\\n3. load the shards: memory-map all 100 indices on\\\\na central machine as 100 OnDiskInvertedLists (a\\\\nmemory map of 83TiB).\\\\nThe central machine that processes queries per-\\\\nforms the coarse quantization and loads the inverted\\\\nlists from the distributed disk partition.\\\\nThe limiting factor is the network bandwidth of the\\\\ncentral machine. Therefore, it is more efficient to dis-\\\\ntribute the search on 20 intermediate servers to spread\\\\nthe load. This brings the search time down to roughly\\\\n1 s per query.\\\\nThis index is built on vanilla Faiss in pure Python,\\\\non commodity CPU servers with hard disk drives and\\\\na regular IP network.\\\\n8.2\\\\nText retrieval\\\\nFaiss is commonly used for natural language process-\\\\ning tasks. In particular, ANNS is relevant for informa-\\\\ntion retrieval [Thakur et al., 2021, Petroni et al., 2021],\\\\nwith applications such as fact checking, entity linking,\\\\nslot filling or open-domain question answering: these\\\\noften rely on retrieving relevant content across a large-\\\\nscale corpus. To that end, embedding models have\\\\nbeen optimized for text retrieval [Izacard et al., 2021,\\\\nLin et al., 2023a].\\\\nFinally,\\\\n[Izacard et al., 2023],\\\\n[Lin et al., 2023b],\\\\n[Shi et al., 2023b] and [Khandelwal et al., 2020] con-\\\\nsist of language models that have been trained to\\\\nintegrate textual retrieval in order to improve their\\\\naccuracy, factuality or compute efficiency.\\\\n8.3\\\\nData mining\\\\nAnother recurrent application of ANNS and Faiss is\\\\nin the mining and curation of large datasets. In par-\\\\nticular, Faiss has been used to mine bilingual texts\\\\nacross very large text datasets retrieved from the web\\\\n[Schwenk and Douze, 2017, Barrault et al., 2023], or to\\\\norganize a language model’s training corpus in order\\\\nto group together series of documents covering simi-\\\\nlar topics [Shi et al., 2023a].\\\\nIn the image domain, [Oquab et al., 2023] leverages\\\\nFaiss to remove duplicates from a dataset containing\\\\n1.3B images.\\\\nIt then relies on efficient indexing in\\\\norder to mine a curated dataset whose distribution\\\\nmatches the distribution of a target dataset.\\\\n8.4\\\\nContent Moderation\\\\nOne of the major applications of Faiss is the de-\\\\ntection and remediation of harmful content at scale.\\\\nHuman labelled examples of policy violating im-\\\\nages and videos are embedded with models such\\\\nas SSCD [Pizzi et al., 2022] and stored in a Faiss in-\\\\ndex. To decide if a new image or video would vio-\\\\nlate some policies, a multi-stage classification pipeline\\\\nfirst embeds the content and searches the Faiss in-\\\\ndex for similar labelled examples, typically utilizing\\\\nrange queries. The results are aggregated and pro-\\\\ncessed through additional machine classification or\\\\nhuman verification. Since the impact of mistakes is\\\\nhigh, good representations should discriminate per-\\\\nceptually similar and different content, and accurate\\\\nsimilarity search is required even at billions to trillion-\\\\nscale.\\\\nThe former problem motivated the Image\\\\nand Video Similarity Challenges [Douze et al., 2021,\\\\nPizzi et al., 2023].\\\\n9\\\\nConclusion\\\\nIn this work, we presented the task of efficient approx-\\\\nimate nearest-neighbor vector search, and exposed\\\\nhow Faiss addresses the most common practitioners’\\\\nproblems in that space. Indeed, Faiss contains a wide\\\\nset of methods that, once combined, achieve varying\\\\ntradeoffs in terms of training time, throughput, mem-\\\\nory usage and accuracy. Most of the use cases and\\\\nexperiments mentioned in this paper are presented\\\\nin more detail and with corresponding code in Faiss’\\\\nwiki pages.\\\\nReferences\\\\n[Amara et al., 2022] Amara, K., Douze, M., Sablay-\\\\nrolles, A., and J´egou, H. Similarly, bitwise identical results are not guaranteed across\\\\nPyTorch releases, individual commits, or different platforms. In particular, CPU and GPU\\\\nresults can be different even for bitwise-identical inputs and even after controlling for\\\\nthe sources of randomness.\\\\n\\\\nBatched computations or slice computations\\\\n------------------------------------------\\\\n\\\\nMany operations in PyTorch support batched computation, where the same operation is performed\\\\nfor the elements of the batches of inputs. An example of this is :meth:`torch.mm` and\\\\n:meth:`torch.bmm`. It is possible to implement batched computation as a loop over batch elements,\\\\nand apply the necessary math operations to the individual batch elements, for efficiency reasons\\\\nwe are not doing that, and typically perform computation for the whole batch. The mathematical\\\\nlibraries that we are calling, and PyTorch internal implementations of operations can produce\\\\nslightly different results in this case, compared to non-batched computations. In particular,\\\\nlet ``A`` and ``B`` be 3D tensors with the dimensions suitable for batched matrix multiplication.\\\\nThen ``(A@B)[0]`` (the first element of the batched result) is not guaranteed to be bitwise\\\\nidentical to ``A[0]@B[0]`` (the matrix product of the first elements of the input batches)\\\\neven though mathematically it's an identical computation.\\\\n\\\\nSimilarly, an operation applied to a tensor slice is not guaranteed to produce results that are\\\\nidentical to the slice of the result of the same operation applied to the full tensor. E.g. let\\\\n``A`` be a 2-dimensional tensor. ``A.sum(-1)[0]`` is not guaranteed to be bitwise equal to\\\\n``A[:,0].sum()``.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nExtremal values\\\\n---------------\\\\n\\\\nWhen inputs contain large values such that intermediate results may overflow the range of the\\\\nused datatype, the end result may overflow too, even though it is representable in the original\\\\ndatatype. E.g.:\\\\n\\\\n.. code:: python\\\\n\\\\n    import torch\\\\n    a=torch.tensor([1e20, 1e20]) # fp32 type by default\\\\n    a.norm() # produces tensor(inf)\\\\n    a.double().norm() # produces tensor(1.4142e+20, dtype=torch.float64), representable in fp32\\\\n\\\\n.. _Linear Algebra Stability:\\\\n\\\\nLinear algebra (``torch.linalg``)\\\\n---------------------------------\\\\n\\\\nNon-finite values\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nThe external libraries (backends) that ``torch.linalg`` uses provide no guarantees on their behaviour\\\\nwhen the inputs have non-finite values like ``inf`` or ``NaN``. As such, neither does PyTorch.\\\\nThe operations may return a tensor with non-finite values, or raise an exception, or even segfault.\\\\n\\\\nConsider using :func:`torch.isfinite` before calling these functions to detect this situation.\\\\n\\\\nExtremal values in linalg\\\\n\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nFunctions within ``torch.linalg`` have more `Extremal Values`_ than other PyTorch functions.\\\\n\\\\n:ref:`linalg solvers` and :ref:`linalg inverses` assume that the input matrix ``A`` is invertible. If it is close to\\\\nbeing non-invertible (for example, if it has a very small singular value), then these algorithms may silently return\\\\nincorrect results. These matrices are said to be `ill-conditioned <https://nhigham.com/2020/03/19/what-is-a-condition-number/>`_.\\\\nIf provided with ill-conditioned inputs, the result of these functions they may vary when using the same inputs on different\\\\ndevices or when using different backends via the keyword ``driver``.\\\\n\\\\nSpectral operations like ``svd``, ``eig``, and ``eigh`` may also return incorrect results (and their gradients may be infinite)\\\\nwhen their inputs have singular values that are close to each other. This is because the algorithms used to compute these decompositions\\\\nstruggle to converge for these inputs.\\\\n\\\\nRunning the computation in ``float64`` (as NumPy does by default) often helps, but it does not solve these issues in all cases.\\\\nAnalyzing the spectrum of the inputs via :func:`torch.linalg.svdvals` or their condition number via :func:`torch.linalg.cond`\\\\nmay help to detect these issues.\\\\n\\\\n\\\\nTensorFloat-32(TF32) on Nvidia Ampere (and later) devices\\\\n---------------------------------------------------------\\\\n\\\\nOn Ampere (and later) Nvidia GPUs, PyTorch can use TensorFloat32 (TF32) to speed up mathematically intensive operations, in particular matrix multiplications and convolutions.\\\\nWhen an operation is performed using TF32 tensor cores, only the first 10 bits of the input mantissa are read.\\\\nThis may reduce accuracy and produce surprising results (e.g., multiplying a matrix by the identity matrix may produce results that are different from the input).\\\\nBy default, TF32 tensor cores are disabled for matrix multiplications and enabled for convolutions, although most neural network workloads have the same convergence behavior when using TF32 as they have with fp32.\\\\nWe recommend enabling TF32 tensor cores for matrix multiplications with ``torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = \\\\\\\"tf32\\\\\\\"`` (```torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = True`` is going to be deprecated) if your network does not need full float32 precision.\\\\nIf your network needs full float32 precision for both matrix multiplications and convolutions, then TF32 tensor cores can also be disabled for convolutions with ``torch.backends.cudnn.conv.fp32_precision = \\\\\\\"ieee\\\\\\\"`` (``torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 = False`` is going to be deprecated).\\\\n\\\\nFor more information see :ref:`TensorFloat32<tf32_on_ampere>`.\\\\n\\\\nReduced Precision Reduction for FP16 and BF16 GEMMs\\\\n----------------------------------------------------\\\\nHalf-precision GEMM operations are typically done with intermediate accumulations (reduction) in single-precision for numerical accuracy and improved resilience to overflow. For performance, certain GPU architectures, especially more recent ones, allow a few truncations of the intermediate accumulation results to the reduced precision (e.g., half-precision). This change is often benign from the perspective of model convergence, though it may lead to unexpected results (e.g., ``inf`` values when the final result should be be representable in half-precision).\\\\nIf reduced-precision reductions are problematic, they can be turned off with\\\\n``torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction = False``\\\\n\\\\nA similar flag exists for BF16 GEMM operations and is turned on by default. If BF16\\\\nreduced-precision reductions are problematic, they can be turned off with\\\\n``torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction = False``\\\\n\\\\nFor more information see :ref:`allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction<fp16reducedprecision>` and :ref:`allow_bf16_reduced_precision_reduction<bf16reducedprecision>`\\\\n\\\\nReduced Precision Reduction for FP16 and BF16 in Scaled Dot Product Attention (SDPA)\\\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\nA naive SDPA math backend, when using FP16/BF16 inputs, can accumulate significant numerical errors due to the usage of low-precision intermediate buffers. To mitigate this issue, the default behavior now involves upcasting FP16/BF16 inputs to FP32. Computations are performed in FP32/TF32, and the final FP32 results are then downcasted back to FP16/BF16. This will improve numerical accuracy of the final output for the math backend with FP16/BF16 inputs, but increases memory usages and may cause the performance regressions in the math backend as computations shift from FP16/BF16 BMM to FP32/TF32 BMM/Matmul.\\\\n\\\\nFor scenarios where reduced-precision reductions are preferred for speed, they can be enabled with the following setting:\\\\n``torch.backends.cuda.allow_fp16_bf16_reduction_math_sdp(True)``\\\\n\\\\n.. _fp16_on_mi200:\\\\n\\\\nReduced Precision FP16 and BF16 GEMMs and Convolutions on AMD Instinct MI200 devices\\\\n------------------------------------------------------------------------------------\\\\nOn AMD Instinct MI200 GPUs, the FP16 and BF16 V_DOT2 and MFMA matrix instructions flush input and output denormal values to zero. FP32 and FP64 MFMA matrix instructions do not flush input and output denormal values to zero. The affected instructions are only used by rocBLAS (GEMM) and MIOpen (convolution) kernels; all other PyTorch operations will not encounter this behavior. All other supported AMD GPUs will not encounter this behavior.\\\\n\\\\nrocBLAS and MIOpen provide alternate implementations for affected FP16 operations. Alternate implementations for BF16 operations are not provided; BF16 numbers have a larger dynamic range than FP16 numbers and are less likely to encounter denormal values. For the FP16 alternate implementations, FP16 input values are cast to an intermediate BF16 value and then cast back to FP16 output after the accumulate FP32 operations. In this way, the input and output types are unchanged.\\\\n\\\\nWhen training using FP16 precision, some models may fail to converge with FP16 denorms flushed to zero. Denormal values more frequently occur in the backward pass of training during gradient calculation. PyTorch by default will use the rocBLAS and MIOpen alternate implementations during the backward pass. The default behavior can be overridden using environment variables, ROCBLAS_INTERNAL_FP16_ALT_IMPL and MIOPEN_DEBUG_CONVOLUTION_ATTRIB_FP16_ALT_IMPL. The behavior of these environment variables is as follows:\\\\n\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n|               | forward   | backward  |\\\\n+===============+===========+===========+\\\\n| Env unset     | original  | alternate |\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n| Env set to 1  | alternate | alternate |\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n| Env set to 0  | original  | original  |\\\\n+---------------+-----------+-----------+\\\\n\\\\nThe following is the list of operations where rocBLAS may be used:\\\\n\\\\n* torch.addbmm\\\\n* torch.addmm\\\\n* torch.baddbmm\\\\n* torch.bmm\\\\n* torch.mm\\\\n* torch.nn.GRUCell\\\\n* torch.nn.LSTMCell\\\\n* torch.nn.Linear\\\\n* torch.sparse.addmm\\\\n* the following torch._C._ConvBackend implementations:\\\\n\\\\n  * slowNd\\\\n  * slowNd_transposed\\\\n  * slowNd_dilated\\\\n  * slowNd_dilated_transposed\\\\n\\\\nThe Good.\\\\n\\\\nLet's produce.\\\",\\\"format\\\":\\\"unknown\\\",\\\"index\\\":0}]\"},{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"{\\\"chapter\\\":\\\"# K-MODEL-013：Embedding 与重排：编码函数、批量与评分契约\\\\n\\\\nEmbedding 服务把一条输入映射为一个固定维度向量；重排服务把一个查询与候选集合映射为分数或顺序。两者的主要状态是制品、输入变换、中间张量和候选身份，不是自回归 decode 的逐 token KV。理解这条链路的关键，不是记住某个模型名，而是把「哪个函数产生这个向量或分数」与「批次怎样组织执行」分开：前者决定向量空间和评分契约，后者决定 padding、packing、等待、访存和尾延迟。\\\\n\\\\n## 编码函数：输入、输出与状态\\\\n\\\\n设原始输入为 m，固定制品 A 规定模板、tokenizer 或 processor、特殊 token、最大长度、截断策略 τ、pooling、normalize、输出 dtype 和任务头。文本路径可写成\\\\n\\\\nx = Trunc_τ(Encode_A(Render_A(m)))，\\\\n\\\\n其中 Render 生成模板化内容，Encode 完成规范化、分词、特殊 token 与位置构造。有效位置集合为 S={i | mask_i=1}，编码器输出逐 token 隐藏状态\\\\n\\\\nH = Enc_θ(x, mask, segment, position)，\\\\n\\\\n再经 pooling 与可选归一化得到\\\\n\\\\np = Pool_{A,P}(H, S_P)，e = Norm_A(p)。\\\\n\\\\nS_P⊆S 是 pooling 合同允许的位置集合。均值池化的一种明确写法是\\\\n\\\\np = (1/|S_P|) Σ_{i∈S_P} H_i，\\\\n\\\\n分母只含允许位置；是否排除 [CLS]、[SEP] 等特殊 token 属于制品定义，不是由张量形状自动决定。零范数归一化也必须由制品固定：可以拒绝、返回规定零向量，或使用带 ε 的尺度；不同策略不能混用。\\\\n\\\\n| 对象 | 含义 | 不能由它推出 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| θ、A | 权重、tokenizer、pooling、normalize、dtype、任务头 | 相同维度就属于同一向量空间 |\\\\n| x、mask、segment、position | 本次有效输入与可见位置 | 物理张量宽度等于有效长度 |\\\\n| H | 逐 token 隐藏状态 | 任意一列都适合作为句向量 |\\\\n| p | pooling 后的向量 | normalize 已经执行 |\\\\n| e、序列化结果 | 绑定完整编码函数的输出向量 | 另一个 pooling 或截断仍得到同一身份 |\\\\n| 批元数据 | request_id、candidate_id、原始序号、截断记录 | 分数可以脱离候选身份 |\\\\n| 索引条目 | id、向量、制品版本、材料映射 | 索引库自动提供完整服务一致性 |\\\\n| 重排分数 | 查询—候选评分头的输出 | 可以当作普通双塔内积接口 |\\\\n\\\\n固定 BERT v1 描述的是多层双向 Transformer encoder；输入表示由 token、segment 和 position embedding 相加，句对打包为一个序列并用 [SEP] 与 segment A/B 区分，[CLS] 的末层隐藏状态被用作分类任务的聚合表示。固定 v1 还给出 WordPiece 词表与最长 512 token 的配置。这些事实支持双向可见性与句对输入的结构，不证明未经相应训练的 [CLS]、任意均值池化或任意层拼接天然适合语义检索；pooling 与评分头必须作为训练制品的一部分看待。\\\\n\\\\n同一文档从 128 个 token 截断到 64 个 token，会改变剩余 token 可见的左右上下文，因而不只是丢掉后半段输出。双向编码器通常不能把前 64 个 token 的深层状态当作更长输入未来追加部分的精确前缀缓存。可缓存的独立文档向量必须绑定完整有效输入、截断范围、pooling、normalize 和编码器版本。\\\\n\\\\n## 双塔、交叉编码器与评分契约\\\\n\\\\n双塔分别计算 e_q=f_q(q)、e_d=f_d(d)，再用内积、余弦或任务指定的距离评分。双塔权重可以共享，也可以不同，但索引侧与查询侧必须遵循训练好的配套契约；相同维度只证明张量能相乘，不证明两个坐标空间兼容。常用的三个评分关系是\\\\n\\\\ns_IP(a,b)=a·b，\\\\n\\\\ns_cos(a,b)=(a·b)/(||a||_2 ||b||_2)，\\\\n\\\\nd_2²(a,b)=||a-b||_2²=||a||_2²+||b||_2²-2a·b。\\\\n\\\\n余弦在零范数处没有定义，必须按合同拒绝、返回规定值或使用带 ε 的近似；不能默默产生 NaN 后继续排序。若双方都按同一规则归一化为单位向量，则内积等于余弦，平方 L2 等于 2-2a·b，因此按内积降序、按平方 L2 升序和按余弦降序在该前提下给出相同排序。只有查询侧归一化而文档侧没有归一化时，这一等价不成立，内积排序仍受文档范数影响。\\\\n\\\\n交叉编码器把 q、d 放入同一次 attention 或同一任务编码，再输出 s(q,d)。每个候选都要经过这条完整计算链，成本随候选数与句对长度增长；文档深层表示通常不能脱离查询独立复用。交叉编码器的分数不是普通双塔内积接口，不能把其 logits 直接塞回向量索引。\\\\n\\\\n一个查询含 k 个候选时，系统可以聚批句对，但必须保留查询身份、候选身份、重复候选的出现序号和原顺序。若输出概率，归一化必须绑定同一查询的固定候选集合和任务头校准；任意跨请求 softmax 会让同一候选的分数依赖一起排队的其他请求。若候选集合被过滤、扩增或换序，集合归一化的概率身份也随之改变。\\\\n\\\\n| 评分方案 | 排序方向 | 合法前提 | 不能推出 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 内积 | 越大越前 | 双塔训练指定内积并保留相应范数语义 | 未归一化时排序与余弦相同 |\\\\n| 余弦 | 越大越前 | 双方非零，归一化规则一致 | 零范数有定义 |\\\\n| L2 距离 | 越小越前 | 距离函数、是否平方与索引一致 | 与内积排序无条件等价 |\\\\n| 交叉编码器 | 由任务头定义 | 每个候选经过完整句对函数 | 可复用独立文档向量 |\\\\n\\\\n## 完整算法：批量编码与候选重排\\\\n\\\\n下面的伪代码把逻辑函数、批布局和身份提交放在同一条路径中。布局、桶大小、是否 packing、是否融合 attention 都是方案选择；无论怎样执行，有效输入、mask、pooling 分母、候选映射和输出身份都不能改变。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 EncodeBatch(请求集合 R, 制品 A, 布局策略 L, 容量上限)\\\\n输入：每个请求含 identity、原始内容、文档或候选 ID（如有）、期望输出格式；\\\\n      固定 A 的模板、tokenizer、特殊 token、截断 τ、pooling、normalize、dtype\\\\n输出：每个请求的向量与身份记录，或逐请求错误；不得返回未绑定身份的向量\\\\n1. 核对 A 的模型、tokenizer、pooling、normalize、dtype 与请求声明一致；\\\\n   不兼容制品不得混在同一编码批中。\\\\n2. 对每个请求 r：\\\\n   2.1 m_r ← Render_A(content_r)\\\\n   2.2 x_r ← Trunc_τ(Encode_A(m_r))\\\\n   2.3 记录删除范围、有效长度 n_r、特殊 token、segment 与 position；\\\\n       若 n_r=0 且合同不允许空输入，标记 r 失败；否则进入空输入合同。\\\\n   2.4 计算内容身份 key_r；key 至少含 A、完整有效输入、τ、pooling、\\\\n       normalize、dtype 和任务头。散列键不能替代完整输入校验。\\\\n3. 将可兼容请求分组；每组选择右 padding、左 padding 或带边界的 packing。\\\\n   建立 token 缓冲、valid mask、segment、positions 与序列边界；\\\\n   不同请求不得进入同一双向可见域。容量不足时等待、缩小批或拒绝，\\\\n   不得静默改变已声明的完整输入。\\\\n4. 按层执行 encoder。Q/K/V 与 attention 只读取同一请求的合法位置；\\\\n   等待本层必要写入与读取完成后再推进下一层。\\\\n   融合实现可以避免完整分数矩阵，但不能改变逻辑可见集合。\\\\n5. 对每个成功请求 r：\\\\n   5.1 S_r ← valid mask 与 pooling 合同允许的位置；\\\\n       是否排除特殊 token 由 A 固定。\\\\n   5.2 若 S_r 为空：按 A 的空池化合同失败或返回规定值。\\\\n   5.3 p_r ← Pool_A(H_r, S_r)；例如均值池化分母为 |S_r|。\\\\n   5.4 e_r ← Normalize_A(p_r)；ε、dtype 与零范数策略固定。\\\\n   5.5 按输出格式序列化 e_r，并绑定 request_id、内容 key、A、\\\\n       截断记录和本批物理布局记录。\\\\n6. 只有本请求的输出完整产生后才标记成功；部分失败不得用其他请求结果填充。\\\\n   等待全部必要读取结束后释放输入、激活和工作区，保留审计记录。\\\\n7. 返回向量、有效长度、截断记录、缓存 key 与批次映射。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n编码算法的正确性不变量是：每个有效 token 都来自本请求的同一有效输入；不同请求在 packing 后没有双向可见边；每个池化位置属于 S_P；每个输出向量绑定自己的 request_id 和内容身份。批大小、padding 宽度或 kernel 选择改变时，这些关系仍应保留。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 RerankBatch(q, 候选集合 C, 评分头 S, topk, tie_rule)\\\\n输入：查询 q；候选可重复，但每项有 candidate_id 与 occurrence；\\\\n      每项保留原始 ordinal；评分头 S 的 tokenizer、截断与校准合同固定\\\\n输出：按查询候选集合身份绑定的 top-k、完整分数或逐候选错误\\\\n1. 校验 q、C 与 S 的制品版本；候选为空时返回空结果，不调用评分头。\\\\n2. 对每个 (c, occurrence)：\\\\n   按 S 的模板与截断构造句对输入，记录有效长度和截断范围；\\\\n   若 S 是交叉编码器，不得把文档深层状态脱离 q 复用；\\\\n   若 S 是双塔，则按双塔合同取向量并核对索引/查询侧兼容性。\\\\n3. 形成评分行 row→(query_id, candidate_id, occurrence, ordinal)。\\\\n   聚批时保持该映射；不同查询之间的 attention 不得互相可见。\\\\n   同一查询的候选是否互相可见由评分头定义，通常独立评分。\\\\n4. 执行 S，取得原始分数或 logits z_(q,c)。\\\\n   若输出概率，只在固定 query 的固定候选集合内应用校准与 softmax；\\\\n   候选集合身份改变时，旧概率不得继续使用。\\\\n5. 将每个分数写回其 (candidate_id, occurrence)，不得只按行号写回。\\\\n   若排序方向是距离，则按距离升序；若是相似度，则按降序。\\\\n6. 同一查询内排序：主键为分数，同分按预先声明的 tie_rule，\\\\n   例如原始 ordinal、候选 ID 或稳定出现序号；重复候选保留 multiplicity。\\\\n7. 返回 top-k、完整分数、查询候选集合身份和失败项；\\\\n   部分失败不得伪装成低分候选，也不得让另一个查询的分数填补。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n候选数为 k、每个句对长度为 m_c 时，交叉编码器的主要计算随 Σ_c m_c 的线性层工作和 Σ_c m_c² 的 attention 工作增长；聚批只改变这些工作的组织，不把候选数从成本中消掉。若为了降低候选数而缩小候选集合，那是召回或评分算法变化，必须与只改变聚批的执行优化分开报告。\\\\n\\\\n## Padding、Packing 与计算形状\\\\n\\\\n设一批有 B 条序列，长度 n_i，隐藏维 d，层数 L，head 数 H，每 head 维 d_h，FFN 宽 d_ff，有效 token 数 N_tok=Σ_i n_i，最大长度 L_max。线性投影的主要计算可写为\\\\n\\\\nC_lin ≈ Σ_layers 2 N_tok d_in,l d_out,l。\\\\n\\\\n在标准 encoder 层、QKV 合并、FFN 宽 4d 且 H d_h=d 的设定下，主项约为每层 24 N_tok d² FLOP：QKV 约 6N_tok d²、输出投影约 2N_tok d²、两层 FFN 约 16N_tok d²。其他归一化、激活、bias、softmax 和残差另计。双向 attention 的合法配对数若按每个位置与同一序列所有位置配对，则\\\\n\\\\nA_valid=Σ_i n_i²。\\\\n\\\\n统一 padding 到 L_max 后，密集双向 attention 的桶式配对数为\\\\n\\\\nA_bucket=B L_max²。\\\\n\\\\n若把 N_tok 个 token 直接拼成一个连续块并执行完整双向 attention，配对数是 N_tok²；只有 backend 真正表达块对角可见性时，逻辑工作才是 Σ n_i²。逻辑配对、实际执行配对和内存事务必须分开：mask 掉跨序列边不等于硬件没有为这些位置分配或读取存储。\\\\n\\\\nC12-A 的设定仍取四条 64 token 与四条 512 token 序列，d=768，FP32。有效 token 数为 2304；统一 512 桶的线性行数为 4096，二者之比为 4096/2304≈1.7778。有效双向配对为\\\\n\\\\n4×64²+4×512²=1,064,960，\\\\n\\\\n统一 512 桶的密集配对为\\\\n\\\\n8×512²=2,097,152，\\\\n\\\\n比值约 1.9692。若把 2304 个 token 拼成一个完整双向块，则得到 2304²=5,308,416 对，约是有效配对的 4.984 倍；这正是 packing 必须保留边界和块对角可见性的原因。\\\\n\\\\n对于 BERT-base 的 12 层、12 head、每 head 64 维设定，attention 主项可估为 4 L d A_valid，即约 4×12×768×1,064,960≈39.3 GFLOP，仅含 QK 与 PV 的乘加，不含 softmax、mask、归一化和 FFN。该数字是声明条件下的逻辑估算，不是目标设备实测。\\\\n\\\\n若一层显式保存所有 head 的完整分数矩阵，元素数约为 B H L_max²；B=8、H=12、L_max=512、每元素 4 字节时为 8×12×512²×4=100,663,296 字节，约 96 MiB。只保存有效配对时元素数约为 H A_valid，字节数约 48.75 MiB，但真正的随机访问和写回还取决于布局。融合 attention 可以避免完整矩阵驻留，但不能把二次算术变成线性，也不能自动消除 workspace 和同步。\\\\n\\\\n均值池化的计算主项为 O(N_tok d)，输出向量为 B d_out s_out 字节。八个 768 维 FP32 向量为 8×768×4=24,576 字节。若把逐 token 隐藏状态全部回传，则为 B L_max d s；同一设定下为 8×512×768×4=12,582,912 字节，约 12 MiB，是 pooled 输出的 512 倍。只需要句向量时，尽早池化并释放逐 token 激活通常比复制全部隐藏状态更有意义。\\\\n\\\\n重排的交叉编码器成本要按句对而不是按文档一次编码计。设查询长度为 n_q，候选长度为 n_c，模板额外位置为 r_c，则句对长度 m_c=n_q+n_c+r_c；候选总成本主项随 Σ_c m_c 的线性工作和 Σ_c m_c² 的 attention 工作增长。把 20 个候选聚成一批，仍要做 20 条句对；它减少的是提交、权重复用和填充浪费，不是候选评分本身。若评分头是双塔内积，成本可降到 O(k d) 量级，但这就不是交叉编码器质量/成本方案。\\\\n\\\\n## 缓存、驻留与阶段预算\\\\n\\\\nEmbedding 向量缓存的身份至少包含：编码器与任务头版本、tokenizer 或 processor、模板与特殊 token、完整有效输入、截断策略与实际删除范围、pooling、normalize、输出 dtype、距离或评分度量。重排分数缓存还要包含查询身份、候选身份与出现序号、评分头版本；若概率按候选集合归一化，还要包含集合身份和集合顺序。只保存内容散列而不校验完整输入，会把散列碰撞当成同一向量；只保存前缀而忽略截断，会把不同上下文当成同一文档。\\\\n\\\\n六类成本可以这样列账。计算包括线性投影、attention、softmax、pooling、归一化、候选评分和排序；访存包括权重、输入、逐层激活、完整或分块的分数矩阵、向量索引、分数缓存和输出；通信包括主机到设备的 ID、mask、位置，以及设备到主机的 pooled 向量或分数，若要回传全部隐藏状态则另算；准备包括 tokenizer、模板、聚批、桶选择、索引构建/训练、缓存装载和编译；同步包括一次 forward 的完成事件、主机读取设备结果、候选提交和失败回滚；驻留包括权重、workspace、待处理批次、输出队列、唯一文档向量和重排候选缓冲。\\\\n\\\\n一个保守的峰值模型是\\\\n\\\\nM_peak ≈ W_phys + A_work + O_batch + I_pending，\\\\n\\\\n其中各项只按唯一物理对象计一次；共享同一权重或同一文档向量的逻辑引用不能重复相加，而同一内容的两个物理副本仍要分别计。向量索引本体可估为 N_unique d s，重排分数缓存可估为 N_pairs s_score，另有页表、元数据、候选集合映射和失败重试缓冲。若预分配固定池，池总量与池内存活对象不能相加成两个峰值。\\\\n\\\\n端到端延迟由排队、模板与分词、设备搬运、编码或重排、pooling 或分数提交、后处理与归还组成。小批短句可能由 tokenizer、提交和主机同步主导；长句的 attention 与激活更重；大量文档离线建库则更重视吞吐、持久化和失败重试。若主机阶段每请求消耗 c CPU 秒、到达率为 λ、有效核预算为 p，则 λc<p 只是稳定性的必要条件，不能保证 p95 或 p99。没有设备时间线时，不能把逻辑字节直接称为 HBM 事务或实测时延。\\\\n\\\\n在 GPU 映射上，较大的规则线性层和批量距离计算通常更容易利用矩阵单元，较小的批可能转为权重带宽或提交主导；完整分数矩阵会改变片上驻留与 spill。CPU 上则更受线程、NUMA、向量化和主机准备影响。这些是条件化选择，不是某一 tile、某一桶或某一 batch 的通用最优值；本章没有目标 GPU 的实测数据。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化：保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n| 变化 | 可保留 | 必须重算或失效 | 放弃旧结论的条件 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 编码器、tokenizer、模板、pooling、normalize 改变 | 原始内容、任务标签、独立参考 | 文档向量、查询向量、索引身份、缓存键 | 旧向量不再对应同一编码函数 |\\\\n| 截断长度或删除范围改变 | 原始媒体与完整输入 | 受影响文档向量与缓存 | 旧向量的有效上下文已经改变 |\\\\n| dtype、量化、ε 或归一化实现改变 | 数学评分定义与测试输入 | |\\\\n| 候选集合、过滤条件或 top-k 改变 | 查询与材料源 | 集合归一化概率、召回与排序指标 | 为了加速缩小候选却仍宣称只改执行 |\\\\n| 到达分布、等待窗口、在线/离线改变 | 逻辑编码与评分 | 桶选择、batch 形成、队列与驻留 | 等待或 padding 收益超过计算节省 |\\\\n| 重排头从交叉编码器换成双塔 | 查询与候选源 | dtype、数值路径和容差写进身份；若任务要求逐位一致，必须额外证明，而不能只凭数学等价。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断、反例与区分实验\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 区分干预与反证修正 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 同一文本得到不同向量 | 模板、tokenizer、特殊 token、截断、pooling、normalize、dtype 不同 | 服务把一次输入变成固定维度表示，重排服务把一个查询与候选集合变成分数或顺序。它们的主要状态是固定制品、输入变换、有效位置、中间张量和输出身份，不能直接套用自回归 decode 的逐 token KV 生命周期。\\\\n\\\\n## 编码函数、输入输出与状态\\\\n\\\\n固定一个编码制品 A，它至少包含模型权重、tokenizer 与模板、截断规则、特殊 token 与 segment 规则、pooling、可选归一化、输出 dtype 与序列化格式。对原始输入 s，编码结果可写为：\\\\n\\\\n`x = τ_A(s)`，`S = Valid_A(x)`，`H = E_A(x; θ)`，`p = Pool_A(H, S)`，`e = N_A(p)`。\\\\n\\\\n`τ_A` 负责模板、规范化、分词、截断和模态展开；`S` 是参与 pooling 或其他任务头的有效位置集合；`E_A` 是编码器或任务模型；`Pool_A` 可能是 CLS、均值、最后有效位置、加权池化或任务头；`N_A` 可能是 L2 归一化、其他固定变换或恒等。若使用 L2 归一化，一个明确合同是：\\\\n\\\\n当 `‖p‖₂ > ε_A` 时，`N_A(p) = p / ‖p‖₂`；否则按制品合同输出零向量或拒绝，并记录这一分支。\\\\n\\\\n公式中的 `e` 是最终对外向量，但索引侧与查询侧都还必须绑定同一个向量空间、同一距离函数和同一输出格式。输入文本长度相同、输出维度相同，只证明张量形状可以相乘，不证明两个向量含义相同。\\\\n\\\\n状态可分为以下几层：\\\\n\\\\n| 状态 | 含义 | 不能由它推断 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| `A` | 模型、tokenizer、pooling、normalize、dtype 与任务头的固定身份 | 任意同维度模型产生同一向量空间 |\\\\n| `r_i` | 请求、文档、查询或候选的身份与原顺序 | 分数已经属于正确候选 |\\\\n| `x_i, S_i` | 实际有效输入与参与 pooling 的位置 | 物理张量宽度等于有效长度 |\\\\n| `H_i` | 本次编码的层间激活与隐藏状态 | 完成任务后可脱离查询独立复用 |\\\\n| `e_i` | 已提交向量及其编码身份 | 索引版本、材料版本或过滤条件仍一致 |\\\\n| `score_i` | 查询—候选对的分数与评分头身份 | 跨请求可直接比较或作为概率 |\\\\n\\\\nBERT 固定 v1 描述双向 Transformer encoder：一个有效 token 在每层可看到同一输入序列中的左右文。句对可以打包成一个序列，借助 `[SEP]`、segment embedding 与位置表示区分；分类任务可读取 `[CLS]` 的最终隐藏状态。它为 encoder 和句对评分提供结构依据，并不证明未经相应训练或制品声明的 CLS、最后 token 或任意平均池化天然适合语义检索。\\\\n\\\\n截断是编码函数的一部分。把同一文档从长度 128 截断到 64，剩余 token 的可见上下文范围也会改变，因此不只是丢掉后半部分输出。双向编码器通常不能把前 64 个 token 的全部深层状态当作未来追加内容的精确前缀缓存。可缓存的独立文档向量必须绑定完整有效输入、截断结果与完整编码函数。\\\\n\\\\n## 双塔、交叉编码器与评分合法性\\\\n\\\\n双塔检索分别计算 `e_q = f_q(q)` 与 `e_d = f_d(d)`，文档向量可以离线构建，查询只做一次编码并进行向量搜索。两个塔可以共享权重，也可以使用训练得到的两个塔，但索引侧和查询侧必须遵循同一训练契约。共享权重不是自动成立的条件，任意混配两个塔也不能由维度相同来证明合法。\\\\n\\\\n评分函数可以是内积、余弦或训练指定的其他形式。余弦为：\\\\n\\\\n`cos(u,v) = <u,v> / (‖u‖₂‖v‖₂)`，要求双方范数按合同处理。\\\\n\\\\n只有查询和文档都按同一规则归一化后，内积排序才与余弦排序一致；若一方未归一化，内积会受范数影响。零范数必须有明确分支，不能直接做未定义除法。\\\\n\\\\n交叉编码器把 q、d 放入同一次 attention，并由任务头输出 `s(q,d)`。每个候选都要经过这条计算链，成本随候选数及句对长度增长；文档深层表示通常不能脱离查询独立复用。双塔和交叉编码器是不同质量与成本方案，不能把交叉编码器的分数当作普通向量内积接口。\\\\n\\\\n一个请求含 K 个候选时，系统可以把句对聚批，但必须保留查询 ID、候选 ID、原顺序、重复候选的约定及各自截断结果。分数归还错误的候选会表现成模型质量下降。若输出概率，须使用该任务头的校准与归一化定义；任意跨请求 softmax 会让同一候选的分数依赖一起排队的其他请求。若在单个请求的候选集合内做 softmax，候选集合本身也进入评分身份，增加或删除候选会改变所有概率。\\\\n\\\\n重排分数只有在声明了校准与比较域时才可跨查询比较。用于排序的分数、用于阈值的概率和用于质量评估的 nDCG/MRR 是不同对象。稳定同分规则也必须固定，例如按原候选索引或候选 ID 决胜；否则相同分数集合在不同输入顺序下会产生不稳定的输出。\\\\n\\\\n## 批量编码、packing 与状态推进\\\\n\\\\n下面的伪代码给出一个双塔或单塔 batch encoder 的完整数据流。它不指定某个框架或 kernel，只固定输入、有效位置、pooling、归一化和发布边界。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 EncodeBatch\\\\n输入：原始输入 s[0..B−1]、固定制品 A、截断合同 τ、物理宽度 L、批量布局 λ\\\\n输出：向量 e[0..B−1]、每条有效长度/截断/零范数记录，或失败\\\\n\\\\n1. 若 B=0：返回空结果。核对 L 为非负整数；若非空输入需要至少一个位置而 L=0，失败。\\\\n2. 对每个 i：\\\\n   a. 用 A 的模板、规范化与 tokenizer 得到 token 序列；按 τ 截断并记录删除范围。\\\\n   b. n_i ← 有效 token 数。若 n_i=0，按 A 的空输入合同拒绝或走声明的空输入路径。\\\\n   c. 若 n_i>L，失败或选择更大桶；不得静默丢弃有效 token。\\\\n3. 建立物理输入、位置、segment、有效标记与可见性：\\\\n   对每个 i、j<n_i：把 token j 放到 λ(i,j)，设置模型位置与 segment，标记有效。\\\\n   填充槽标记无效；除被合同允许的 padding 计算外，其数值不得进入 pooling 或其他统计。\\\\n   若多个独立请求共享一个 attention 行，可见集合只允许同一请求的有效位置；\\\\n   普通 padding mask 不能替代这种跨序列隔离。\\\\n4. H ← Encoder_A(X, positions, segments, visible)。\\\\n   只有有效位置和同一请求的合法位置进入相应 attention 归约域。\\\\n5. 对每个 i：\\\\n   S_i ← 由 A 的 pooling 合同选出的有效位置集合。\\\\n   若 S_i 为空：失败或走声明的空输入分支。\\\\n   p_i ← Pool_A(H_i, S_i)。\\\\n   nrm ← √(Σ_c p_i,c²)。\\\\n   若 nrm>ε_A：e_i ← p_i/nrm；否则按 A 的零范数合同输出。\\\\n   按 A 执行其他 normalize、dtype 转换与有限性检查。\\\\n6. 在同一提交点发布 e_i 与其编码身份记录；部分批次失败不得覆盖旧版本。\\\\n   只有全部必要步骤完成后，向量才可交给索引、缓存或重排服务。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n正确性不变量包括：批次行置换后按原身份还原应得到同一语义结果；padding 不得进入有效 pooling 分母；packing 后的每个请求不得看到另一请求的 token；同一身份键必须覆盖 tokenizer、有效输入、截断、pooling、normalize、dtype 与任务头。\\\\n\\\\n设一批有 B 个长度 n_i 的序列，物理宽度为 L。双向 encoder 的密集 attention 逻辑配对数，按每层每个序列计算，统一 padding 后约为 `B L²`；按长度分组且不做跨请求 attention 时约为 `Σ_i n_i²`。若把多个序列放入一个连续缓冲，使用块对角可见性可把逻辑配对限制为各序列内部的平方和；仅拼接 token 后做一次全局双向 attention，会让不同请求相互影响。\\\\n\\\\nPooling 应按有效 token 集合计算。平均池化的分母、特殊 token 是否参与、最后有效位置如何确定，都属于模型制品。右 padding 的批中固定取最后一列可能读到 padding；左 padding 或位置重建也不能凭形状猜测其含义。取 CLS 行只有在任务头与 pooling 合同声明它有效时才成立。\\\\n\\\\n```pseudocode\\\\n算法 RerankBatch\\\\n输入：查询 q、候选 D[0..K−1]、交叉编码器制品 A、截断 τ、聚批布局 λ、评分头 H\\\\n输出：每个候选的分数、稳定顺序与身份记录，或失败\\\\n\\\\n1. 若 K=0：返回空结果。核对查询与候选身份；按合同处理重复候选并保留原索引。\\\\n2. 对每个 i：\\\\n   按 A 的句对构造把 q 与 D[i] 放入同一输入；\\\\n   按制品规定设置 segment、特殊 token 与截断；\\\\n   记录 pair_id、候选 ID、实际长度和被删除范围。\\\\n3. 按 λ 聚批。每个 pair 的有效 query 只能看到同一 pair 的合法位置；\\\\n   填充不参与 pooling，也不能成为候选的可见上下文。\\\\n4. s_i ← ScoreHead_A(Encoder_A(pair_i))。\\\\n   若评分头输出概率，则按该头的校准合同执行，不跨请求做未声明的 softmax。\\\\n5. 若合同声明集合归一化，只在该查询的候选集合上执行，并保存集合身份；\\\\n   否则每个候选的分数保持独立。\\\\n6. 按分数降序排序；同分按原索引或候选 ID 的固定规则决胜。\\\\n7. 返回 (doc_id, s_i, rank) 与截断记录。部分失败必须显式记录，\\\\n   不能把缺失候选当作最低分或默认候选。\\\\n```\\\\n\\\\n## 成本：计算、访存、准备、同步与驻留\\\\n\\\\n设有效 token 总数为 `S = Σ_i n_i`，物理宽度为 L，隐藏维为 d，输出维为 d_out。线性投影、FFN 与任务头的主要算术量可写成 `C_lin ≈ c_lin S d²`，其中 `c_lin` 由具体层结构决定；不能用这个符号公式替代某个模型的精确 FLOP 数。\\\\n\\\\n双向 attention 的密集逻辑配对数，按每层每头计算，统一 padding 后为 `A_pad = B L²`，按长度分组或块对角 packing 后为 `A_block = Σ_i n_i²`。每个配对的 QK 与 PV 工作还依赖 head 维和 value 维，记为 `c_pair`，则 attention 主项约为 `c_pair A`。融合 attention 可以避免显式保存完整分数矩阵，但不能因此把算术工作当作线性。\\\\n\\\\n交叉编码器重排有 K 个句对，句对长度为 l_i 时，密集配对数约为 `Σ_i l_i²`；若统一填充到 L，则约为 `K L²`。双塔在线阶段只编码一次查询并进行向量搜索，交叉编码器则对每个候选执行一次句对编码，二者不能只比较搜索时间。减少候选数会同时改变计算量和召回集合，应作为算法变化记录。\\\\n\\\\n输出向量主体为 `B d_out s` 字节，s 是每元素字节数；离线文档向量存储主项为 `N_doc d_out s`，另有 ID、版本、过滤元数据和索引结构。只保存 pooled embedding 而尽早释放逐 token 隐藏状态，通常比向宿主复制全部 token 表示更节省流量，但层间 residual 和 workspace 仍需真实驻留。\\\\n\\\\n成本至少分六类列账：计算包括投影、FFN、attention、pooling 和排序；访存包括权重、激活、向量、索引和元数据；通信包括主机到设备输入、设备回传向量、离线索引写入与远端服务；准备包括 tokenizer、模型加载、索引训练或码本、编译和调优；同步包括批次屏障、设备完成与提交；驻留包括权重、层间激活、attention 工作区、文档向量、缓存和并发请求。\\\\n\\\\n等待聚批会增加在线延迟，统一 padding 会增加无效行工作，按长度分组会增加队列和调度复杂度。命中缓存会减少编码，但可能改变剩余请求的长度分布，不能只用原始流量评估聚批策略。三个负载不宜共用一个每秒 token 指标：在线短查询、长文档离线建库和交叉重排的瓶颈不同。\\\\n\\\\n## 条件变化后的保留、调整与放弃\\\\n\\\\n缓存 key 至少包含编码器与任务头版本、tokenizer 与前处理、完整有效输入、截断与 pooling、normalize、输出 dtype 与序列化格式。重排分数缓存还依赖查询、候选对、评分头和集合评分合同。\\\\n\\\\n| 条件变化 | 可保留 | 必须重算或重验 | 放弃旧结论的条件 |\\\\n|---|---|---|---|\\\\n| 模型、tokenizer、模板或 pooling 改变 | 原始消息、原始文档和外部候选 ID | 有效输入、向量空间、索引向量和校准 | 旧向量不再对应同一编码函数 |\\\\n| 截断规则改变 | 未被截断的短输入身份 | 受影响输入的有效 token 与向量 | 旧 key 只覆盖旧的完整有效输入 |\\\\n| normalize 或输出 dtype 改变 | 原始 pooled 结果若被保留且可追溯 | 归一化、序列化、距离与阈值 | 旧索引与查询侧不再同契约 |\\\\n| 仅 batch 分组或聚批窗口改变 | 输入身份与模型函数 | 数值路径、尾延迟和资源峰值 | 执行组织变化改变了超出容差的排序 |\\\\n| 索引距离、过滤或材料版本改变 | 查询向量，若其编码身份未变 | 候选集合、索引读取和分数解释 | 只命中旧向量而材料已不合法 |\\\\n| 候选数减少 | 同一查询与评分头 | 计算量、召回集合和端到端质量 | 加速来自少算候选而非调度改善 |\\\\n| 设备或精度路径改变 | 数学函数和原始输入 | 数值容差、重排边际和性能 | 未经验证的跨设备逐位一致被否定 |\\\\n\\\\n只有实际有效 token 序列和全部编码字段都相同，才可复用向量；截断策略名称相同不构成证明。仅改变 batch 分组通常不应改变语义身份，但浮点归约路径可能产生容差内差异。若这种差异改变同分附近的选择，应按排序边际与数值契约诊断，而不是直接把 batch 身份写入所有缓存键。\\\\n\\\\n## 诊断：竞争解释、区分实验与反证\\\\n\\\\n| 观察 | 竞争解释 | 可区分的干预与判断 |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| 离线与在线文档向量不同 | tokenizer、模板、截断、pooling、normalize、模型版本或 dtype 不同 | 固定模型与输入，逐层比较渲染字节、token ID、mask、pooled 向量和归一化结果；从第一个不同表示修正归因 |\\\\n| 单条与聚批结果不同 | padding 进入 pooling；packing 跨请求可见；浮点归约差异 | 比较单条、右 padding、左 padding 和批次置换；若只有容差内数值差且排序不变，先按数值路径解释 |\\\\n| 重排后分数像是属于另一个候选 | ID 映射、候选置换、部分失败或缓存错配 | 构造可逆候选置换，检查每个返回 ID 与其原分数；错误配对不能被平均分数掩盖 |\\\\n| 增加一个候选后所有概率改变 | 在候选集合上做 softmax；集合身份进入缓存键 | 固定同一查询与评分头，比较单独一对与整集合的概率；若只做排序，确认是否用了不应使用的集合归一化 |\\\\n| 缓存命中后质量下降 | key 缺少截断、pooling、normalize 或材料版本 | 强制 miss 并从同一输入重算；逐字段对比键与有效输入，不能只比较向量维度 |\\\\n| 量化或压缩后答案变差 | 向量近邻 recall 下降；重排分数变化；候选集合或材料改变 | 固定候选集合先比较向量近邻 recall，再比较交叉重排与最终答案；分开搜索误差和评分误差 |\\\\n| 归一化前后排序翻转 | 内积排序受范数影响；查询和文档未同规则归一化 | 用同一组未归一化向量分别算内积与余弦；q=(1,1)、a=(10,0)、b=(1,1) 时内积偏向 a，余弦偏向 b |\\\\n\\\\n负对照应实际穿过同一比较器。均值池化算例取有效向量 (1,0)、(0,1)，padding 向量 (100,100)，规定均值只含前两行，结果应为 (0.5,0.5)，再 L2 归一化为 (1/√2,1/√2)。若错误地把 padding 放进分母，结果会明显不同，应被独立参考拒绝；固定取最后一列在右 padding 批中也可能读到填充行，应被有效位置参考拒绝。\\\\n\\\\nPacking 的负对照可以构造两个独立序列的块对角可见性，再构造一个错误的全局可见性，让所有有效 token 互相可见。前者应满足同请求内可见、跨请求不可见；后者必须被同一不变量拒绝。只检查最终向量长度无法发现这个错误。\\\\n\\\\n排序的负对照包括同分决胜、候选置换与分数错位。给定分数 a=0.5、b=0.9、c=0.5、d=0.1，按分数降序并以候选 ID 决胜，期望 b、a、c、d；若输入顺序为 d、c、b、a 且实现只做稳定分数排序，可能输出 b、c、a、d，应被固定决胜规则检出。把排序后的 ID 与原始分数列表按位置重新拼接，也会让每个 ID 得到另一个候选的分数，必须由分数—ID 对照拒绝。\\\\n\\\\n这些诊断区分的是机制，而不是一次端到端结果的猜测。若修改 padding mask 后错误消失，支持 padding 泄漏解释；若修改候选置换后错误消失，支持 ID 映射解释；若所有布局都一致而只有低精度路径改变排序，再检查数值边际。\\\\n\\\\n## C12-A：Embedding 与重排的完整验证场景\\\\n\\\\n设定一个已固定输入和 pooling 契约的 encoder，输出 768 维 FP32；在线批含四条 64 token 与四条 512 token 序列。统一 512 桶的 attention 配对数为 `8×512²=2,097,152`，按两类分批后为 `4×64²+4×512²=1,064,960`。约 1.97 倍只是逻辑配对数之比，不包含权重、投影、等待与 kernel 效率，不能直接作为时延加速。线性 token 位置为 `8×512=4,096` 对 `4×64+4×512=2,304`，比例约为 1.78；八个输出向量合计 `8×768×4=24,576` 字节。\\\\n\\\\n候选 A 使用统一桶，在有限等待窗口内组成一个批；候选 B 使用 64/512 两桶并分别设置最大等待时间。质量目标是保持每条输入的编码函数，服务目标是固定 offered workload 下的 p95/p99 响应和完成率。离线建库可放宽等待来提高利用率，在线稀疏到达时则可能选择 A 或更小批。\\\\n\\\\n重排部分为每个查询固定 20 个候选，句对长度设为 288，忽略特殊 token 时密集配对数为 `20×288²=1,658,880`；若 padding 到 320，则为 `20×320²=2,048,000`，多出 389,120 对。这些仍是逻辑配对，不是 GPU 实测时间。把候选数从 20 降到 10 会减少计算，但同时也改变召回集合，不能与只改变聚批的方案混为一谈。\\\\n\\\\n先用单样本参考逐条计算，再对照两种批处理的完整向量、余弦/内积和候选排序。一个独立 pooling 单元算例取有效向量 (1,0)、(0,1)，padding 向量 (100,100)，规定均值只含前两行，结果应为 (0.5,0.5)，再 L2 归一化为 (1/√2,1/√2)。这是测试输入变换的设定算例，不代表任意 checkpoint 应采用均值池化。\\\\n\\\\n重排验证先核对每个 score 与候选身份，再测 nDCG/MRR 或任务规定的相关性指标，不能用向量数值接近代替排序质量。覆盖空文本、只有特殊 token、超长截断、重复候选、同分排序、混合长度、取消一个子请求和部分失败。批量置换后还原顺序应保持语义；固定取最后一列、把 padding 纳入均值、使用跨请求全局 attention 或错配候选分数，都应成为能被独立比较器拒绝的负对照。\\\\n\\\\n最后同时报告编码延迟、完整查询重排延迟、候选数分布、内存峰值与质量。若缩小候选数带来加速，需要把召回损失列为算法变化；若只改变聚批，则使用同一候选集合比较。随章检查的模型范围是 CPU 逻辑模型，覆盖 masked mean pooling、左右 padding、块对角可见性、重排 ID 对齐、同分稳定、余弦/内积区分和缓存键缺失；它不执行真实 Transformer 前向、GPU 内存事务、服务尾延迟或检索质量实验。\\\\n\\\\n<!-- infraagents:provenance -->\\\\n\\\\n## 来源与推导\\\\n\\\\n- [S-BERT：BERT](../sources/S-BERT.md)：固定 v1 描述双向 Transformer encoder、token/segment/position 输入、CLS 句级任务头及句对/序列标注任务。句对被打包为一个序列，并以分隔符与 segment 区分；CLS 的最终隐藏状态服务于分类任务。本章据此限定双向可见性、句对构造和 pooling 身份，不把未训练的 CLS 或任意平均池化归为检索质量保证。\\\\n accuracy](../sources/S-TORCH-NUMERIC.md)：固定文档说明浮点加法与乘法不满足实数运算的全部结合性质，批量方式、切片方式、归约顺序和平台路径可以产生数值差异；数值格式、累加精度、极端输入、TF32 与 reduced-precision reduction 也会改变结果。本章据此不要求跨 batch
